   252→// triggerWingmanReview checks preconditions and spawns the detached review process.
   253→func triggerWingmanReview(payload WingmanPayload) {
   254→	// Prevent infinite recursion: if we're inside a wingman auto-apply,
   255→	// don't trigger another review. The env var is set by triggerAutoApply.
   256→	if os.Getenv("ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY") != "" {
   257→		return
   258→	}
   259→
   260→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "wingman")
   261→	repoRoot := payload.RepoRoot
   262→
   263→	totalFiles := len(payload.ModifiedFiles) + len(payload.NewFiles) + len(payload.DeletedFiles)
   264→	logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman trigger evaluating",
   265→		slog.String("session_id", payload.SessionID),
   266→		slog.Int("file_count", totalFiles),
   267→	)
   268→
   269→	// Check if a pending REVIEW.md already exists for the current session
   270→	if shouldSkipPendingReview(repoRoot, payload.SessionID) {
   271→		logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman skipped: pending review exists for current session")
   272→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Pending review exists, skipping\n")
   273→		return
   274→	}
   275→
   276→	// Atomic lock file prevents concurrent review spawns. O_CREATE|O_EXCL
   277→	// is atomic on all platforms, avoiding the TOCTOU race of Stat+WriteFile.
   278→	lockPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanLockFile)
   279→	if !acquireWingmanLock(lockPath, payload.SessionID) {
   280→		logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman skipped: review already in progress")
   281→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Review in progress, skipping\n")
   282→		return
   283→	}
   284→
   285→	// Dedup check: compute hash of sorted file paths
   286→	allFiles := make([]string, 0, len(payload.ModifiedFiles)+len(payload.NewFiles)+len(payload.DeletedFiles))
   287→	allFiles = append(allFiles, payload.ModifiedFiles...)
   288→	allFiles = append(allFiles, payload.NewFiles...)
   289→	allFiles = append(allFiles, payload.DeletedFiles...)
   290→	filesHash := computeFilesHash(allFiles)
   291→
   292→	state, _ := loadWingmanState() //nolint:errcheck // best-effort dedup
   293→	if state != nil && state.FilesHash == filesHash && state.SessionID == payload.SessionID {
   294→		logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman skipped: dedup hash match",
   295→			slog.String("files_hash", filesHash[:12]),
   296→		)
   297→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Already reviewed these changes, skipping\n")
   298→		return
   299→	}
   300→
   301→	// Capture HEAD at trigger time so the detached review diffs against
   302→	// the correct commit even if HEAD moves during the initial delay.
   303→	payload.BaseCommit = resolveHEAD(repoRoot)
   304→	logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman captured base commit",
   305→		slog.String("base_commit", payload.BaseCommit),
   306→	)
   307→
   308→	// Write payload to a temp file instead of passing as a CLI argument,
   309→	// which can exceed OS argv limits (~128KB Linux, ~256KB macOS) with
   310→	// many files or long prompts.
   311→	payloadJSON, err := json.Marshal(payload)
   312→	if err != nil {
   313→		logging.Error(logCtx, "wingman failed to marshal payload", slog.Any("error", err))
   314→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Failed to marshal payload: %v\n", err)
   315→		_ = os.Remove(lockPath)
   316→		return
   317→	}
   318→	payloadPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, ".entire", "wingman-payload.json")
   319→	//nolint:gosec // G306: payload file is not secrets
   320→	if err := os.WriteFile(payloadPath, payloadJSON, 0o644); err != nil {
   321→		logging.Error(logCtx, "wingman failed to write payload file", slog.Any("error", err))
   322→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Failed to write payload file: %v\n", err)
   323→		_ = os.Remove(lockPath)
   324→		return
   325→	}
   326→
   327→	// Spawn detached review process with path to payload file
   328→	spawnDetachedWingmanReview(repoRoot, payloadPath)
   329→	logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman review spawned",
   330→		slog.String("session_id", payload.SessionID),
   331→		slog.String("base_commit", payload.BaseCommit),
   332→		slog.Int("file_count", totalFiles),
   333→	)
   334→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Review starting in background...\n")
   335→}
   336→
   337→// triggerWingmanFromCommit builds a wingman payload from the HEAD commit and
   338→// triggers a review. Used by the git post-commit hook for manual-commit strategy
   339→// where files are committed by the user (not by SaveChanges).
   340→func triggerWingmanFromCommit() {
   341→	// Prevent infinite recursion: skip if inside wingman auto-apply
   342→	if os.Getenv("ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY") != "" {
   343→		return
   344→	}
   345→	if !settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {
   346→		return
   347→	}
   348→
   349→	repoRoot, err := paths.RepoRoot()
   350→	if err != nil {
   351→		return
   352→	}
   353→
   354→	head := resolveHEAD(repoRoot)
   355→	if head == "" {
   356→		return
   357→	}
   358→
   359→	// Get changed files from the commit
   360→	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
   361→	defer cancel()
   362→	//nolint:gosec // G204: head is from git rev-parse, not user input
   363→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "diff-tree", "--no-commit-id", "--name-status", "-r", head)
   364→	cmd.Dir = repoRoot
   365→	out, err := cmd.Output()
   366→	if err != nil || len(out) == 0 {
   367→		return
   368→	}
   369→
   370→	var modified, newFiles, deleted []string
   371→	for _, line := range strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(string(out)), "\n") {
   372→		if len(line) < 3 {
   373→			continue
   374→		}
   375→		status := line[0]
   376→		file := strings.TrimSpace(line[1:])
   377→		switch status {
   378→		case 'M':
   379→			modified = append(modified, file)
   380→		case 'A':
   381→			newFiles = append(newFiles, file)
   382→		case 'D':
   383→			deleted = append(deleted, file)
   384→		}
   385→	}
   386→
   387→	if len(modified)+len(newFiles)+len(deleted) == 0 {
   388→		return
   389→	}
   390→
   391→	// Get commit message
   392→	//nolint:gosec // G204: head is from git rev-parse, not user input
   393→	msgCmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "log", "-1", "--format=%B", head)
   394→	msgCmd.Dir = repoRoot
   395→	msgOut, _ := msgCmd.Output() //nolint:errcheck // best-effort commit message
   396→	commitMessage := strings.TrimSpace(string(msgOut))
   397→
   398→	sessionID := strategy.FindMostRecentSession()
   399→
   400→	triggerWingmanReview(WingmanPayload{
   401→		SessionID:     sessionID,
   402→		RepoRoot:      repoRoot,
   403→		ModifiedFiles: modified,
   404→		NewFiles:      newFiles,
   405→		DeletedFiles:  deleted,
   406→		CommitMessage: commitMessage,
   407→	})
   408→}
   409→
   410→// staleLockThreshold is how old a lock file can be before we consider it stale
   411→// (e.g., the detached process was SIGKILLed and the defer never ran).
   412→const staleLockThreshold = 30 * time.Minute
   413→
   414→// acquireWingmanLock atomically creates the lock file. Returns true if acquired.
   415→// If the lock already exists but is older than staleLockThreshold, it is removed
   416→// and re-acquired (handles crashed detached processes).
   417→func acquireWingmanLock(lockPath, sessionID string) bool {
   418→	//nolint:gosec // G304: lockPath is constructed from repoRoot + constant
   419→	f, err := os.OpenFile(lockPath, os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREATE|os.O_EXCL, 0o644)
   420→	if err != nil {
   421→		if !errors.Is(err, os.ErrExist) {
   422→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Failed to create lock: %v\n", err)
   423→			return false
   424→		}
   425→		// Lock exists — check if it's stale
   426→		info, statErr := os.Stat(lockPath)
   427→		if statErr != nil || time.Since(info.ModTime()) <= staleLockThreshold {
   428→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Review already in progress, skipping\n")
   429→			return false
   430→		}
   431→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Removing stale lock (age: %s)\n",
   432→			time.Since(info.ModTime()).Round(time.Second))
   433→		_ = os.Remove(lockPath)
   434→		// Retry the atomic create
   435→		//nolint:gosec // G304: lockPath is constructed from repoRoot + constant
   436→		f, err = os.OpenFile(lockPath, os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREATE|os.O_EXCL, 0o644)
   437→		if err != nil {
   438→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Failed to create lock after stale removal: %v\n", err)
   439→			return false
   440→		}
   441→	}
   442→	_, _ = f.WriteString(sessionID) //nolint:errcheck // best-effort session ID write
   443→	_ = f.Close()
   444→	return true
   445→}
   446→
   447→// resolveHEAD returns the current HEAD commit hash, or empty string on error.
   448→func resolveHEAD(repoRoot string) string {
   449→	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
   450→	defer cancel()
   451→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-parse", "HEAD")
   452→	cmd.Dir = repoRoot
   453→	out, err := cmd.Output()
   454→	if err != nil {
   455→		return ""
   456→	}
   457→	return strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
   458→}
   459→
   460→// computeFilesHash returns a SHA256 hex digest of the sorted file paths.
   461→// Uses null byte separator (impossible in filenames) to avoid ambiguity.
   462→func computeFilesHash(files []string) string {
   463→	sorted := make([]string, len(files))
   464→	copy(sorted, files)
   465→	sort.Strings(sorted)
   466→	h := sha256.Sum256([]byte(strings.Join(sorted, "\x00")))
   467→	return hex.EncodeToString(h[:])
   468→}

   470→// loadWingmanState loads the wingman state from .entire/wingman-state.json.
   471→func loadWingmanState() (*WingmanState, error) {
   472→	statePath, err := paths.AbsPath(wingmanStateFile)
   473→	if err != nil {
   474→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolving wingman state path: %w", err)
   475→	}
   476→
   477→	data, err := os.ReadFile(statePath) //nolint:gosec // path is repo-relative
   478→	if err != nil {
   479→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("reading wingman state: %w", err)
   480→	}
   481→
   482→	var state WingmanState
   483→	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &state); err != nil {
   484→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("parsing wingman state: %w", err)
   485→	}
   486→	return &state, nil
   487→}

   489→// saveWingmanState saves the wingman state to .entire/wingman-state.json.
   490→func saveWingmanState(state *WingmanState) error {
   491→	statePath, err := paths.AbsPath(wingmanStateFile)
   492→	if err != nil {
   493→		return fmt.Errorf("resolving wingman state path: %w", err)
   494→	}
   495→
   496→	dir := filepath.Dir(statePath)
   497→	if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o750); err != nil {
   498→		return fmt.Errorf("creating wingman state directory: %w", err)
   499→	}
   500→
   501→	data, err := json.MarshalIndent(state, "", "  ")
   502→	if err != nil {
   503→		return fmt.Errorf("marshaling wingman state: %w", err)
   504→	}
   505→
   506→	//nolint:gosec // G306: state file is config, not secrets
   507→	if err := os.WriteFile(statePath, data, 0o644); err != nil {
   508→		return fmt.Errorf("writing wingman state: %w", err)
   509→	}
   510→	return nil
   511→}

   528→// newWingmanApplyCmd returns a hidden subcommand used by the stop hook to
   529→// apply a pending REVIEW.md via claude --continue in a detached subprocess.
   530→func newWingmanApplyCmd() *cobra.Command {
   531→	return &cobra.Command{
   532→		Use:    "__apply",
   533→		Hidden: true,
   534→		Args:   cobra.ExactArgs(1),
   535→		RunE: func(_ *cobra.Command, args []string) error {

   541→// shouldSkipPendingReview checks whether a pending REVIEW.md should prevent
   542→// a new review from being triggered. It cleans up stale/orphaned reviews.
   543→//
   544→// Returns true only when REVIEW.md exists AND belongs to the current session
   545→// AND is younger than wingmanStaleReviewTTL.
   546→func shouldSkipPendingReview(repoRoot, currentSessionID string) bool {
   547→	reviewPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)
   548→	if _, err := os.Stat(reviewPath); err != nil {
   549→		return false // No REVIEW.md, don't skip
   550→	}
   551→
   552→	// REVIEW.md exists — check state to determine if it's current or stale
   553→	state := loadWingmanStateDirect(repoRoot)
   554→	if state == nil {
   555→		// Orphan: REVIEW.md without state file — clean up
   556→		_ = os.Remove(reviewPath)
   557→		return false
   558→	}
   559→
   560→	if state.SessionID != currentSessionID {
   561→		// Different session — stale review, clean up
   562→		_ = os.Remove(reviewPath)
   563→		return false
   564→	}
   565→
   566→	if time.Since(state.ReviewedAt) > wingmanStaleReviewTTL {
   567→		// Same session but too old — clean up
   568→		_ = os.Remove(reviewPath)
   569→		return false
   570→	}
   571→
   572→	return true // Current session, fresh review — skip
   573→}
   574→

  "content": "// wingman_lifecycle.go contains wingman integration hooks for the lifecycle dispatcher.\n// These functions are called from lifecycle.go event handlers to inject wingman\n// review state into session start banners, turn start context, and turn end actions.\npackage cli\n\nimport (\n\t\"context\"\n\t\"fmt\"\n\t\"log/slog\"\n\t\"os\"\n\t\"path/filepath\"\n\t\"time\"\n\n\t\"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/logging\"\n\t\"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/paths\"\n\t\"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/settings\"\n\t\"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy\"\n)\n\n// wingmanNotificationLockThreshold is the maximum lock file age for showing\n// \"Reviewing your changes...\" notifications. Much tighter than staleLockThreshold\n// (used for lock acquisition) because a real review takes at most\n// wingmanInitialDelay (10s) + wingmanReviewTimeout (5m) ≈ 6 minutes.\n// A lock older than this is almost certainly stale for notification purposes.\nconst wingmanNotificationLockThreshold = 10 * time.Minute\n\n// appendWingmanSessionStartStatus appends wingman status to the session start banner.\n// Returns the message with wingman status appended.\nfunc appendWingmanSessionStartStatus(message string) string {\n\tif !settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {\n\t\treturn message\n\t}\n\n\trepoRoot, rootErr := paths.RepoRoot()\n\tif rootErr != nil {\n\t\treturn message + \"\\n  Wingman is active: your changes will be automatically reviewed.\"\n\t}\n\n\tif _, statErr := os.Stat(filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)); statErr == nil {\n\t\treturn message + \"\\n  Wingman: a review is pending and will be addressed on your next prompt.\"\n\t}\n\treturn message + \"\\n  Wingman is active: your changes will be automatically reviewed.\"\n}\n\n// handleWingmanTurnStart checks for a pending wingman review and injects it\n// as additionalContext so the agent addresses it before the user's request.\n// Returns true if a hook response was written to stdout (caller should return early).\nfunc handleWingmanTurnStart(sessionID string) bool {\n\tif !settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\n\trepoRoot, rootErr := paths.RepoRoot()\n\tif rootErr != nil {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\n\twingmanLogCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), \"wingman\")\n\n\t// If a review is pending, inject it as additionalContext\n\tif _, statErr := os.Stat(filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)); statErr == nil {\n\t\tfmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, \"[wingman] Review available: .entire/REVIEW.md — injecting into context\\n\")\n\t\tlogging.Info(wingmanLogCtx, \"wingman injecting review instruction on prompt-submit\",\n\t\t\tslog.String(\"session_id\", sessionID),\n\t\t)\n\t\tif err := outputHookResponseWithContextAndMessage(\n\t\t\twingmanApplyInstruction,\n\t\t\t\"[Wingman] A code review is pending and will be addressed before your request.\",\n\t\t); err != nil {\n\t\t\tfmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, \"[wingman] Warning: failed to inject review instruction: %v\\n\", err)\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\treturn true // Hook response written to stdout — caller must return\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Notify if a review is currently in progress (fresh lock file).\n\tlockPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanLockFile)\n\tif lockInfo, statErr := os.Stat(lockPath); statErr == nil && time.Since(lockInfo.ModTime()) <= wingmanNotificationLockThreshold {\n\t\tlogging.Info(wingmanLogCtx, \"wingman review in progress\",\n\t\t\tslog.String(\"session_id\", sessionID),\n\t\t)\n\t\tif err := outputHookMessage(\"[Wingman] Review in progress...\"); err != nil {\n\t\t\tfmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, \"[wingman] Warning: failed to output review-in-progress message: %v\\n\", err)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn false\n}\n\n// handleWingmanTurnEnd handles wingman actions at turn end: triggering reviews,\n// auto-applying pending reviews, and showing stop notifications.\nfunc handleWingmanTurnEnd(sessionID string, totalChanges int, relModifiedFiles, relNewFiles, relDeletedFiles, allPrompts []string, commitMessage string) {\n\trepoRoot, err := paths.RepoRoot()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\tstrat := GetStrategy()\n\n\t// Trigger wingman review for auto-commit strategy (commit already happened\n\t// in SaveStep). Manual-commit triggers wingman from the git post-commit hook\n\t// instead, since the user commits manually.\n\tif totalChanges > 0 && strat.Name() == strategy.StrategyNameAutoCommit && settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {\n\t\ttriggerWingmanReview(WingmanPayload{\n\t\t\tSessionID:     sessionID,\n\t\t\tRepoRoot:      repoRoot,\n\t\t\tModifiedFiles: relModifiedFiles,\n\t\t\tNewFiles:      relNewFiles,\n\t\t\tDeletedFiles:  relDeletedFiles,\n\t\t\tPrompts:       allPrompts,\n\t\t\tCommitMessage: commitMessage,\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\n\t// Auto-apply pending wingman review on turn end\n\ttriggerWingmanAutoApplyIfPending(repoRoot)\n\n\toutputWingmanStopNotification(repoRoot)\n}\n\n// triggerWingmanAutoApplyIfPending checks for a pending REVIEW.md and spawns\n// the auto-apply subprocess if conditions are met. Called from the stop hook\n// on every turn end (both with-changes and no-changes paths).\n//\n// When a live session exists, this is a no-op: the prompt-submit injection\n// will deliver the review visibly in the user's terminal instead. Background\n// auto-apply is only used when no sessions are alive (all ended).\nfunc triggerWingmanAutoApplyIfPending(repoRoot string) {\n\tlogCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), \"wingman\")\n\tif !settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {\n\t\tlogging.Debug(logCtx, \"wingman auto-apply skip: wingman not enabled\")\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tif os.Getenv(\"ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY\") != \"\" {\n\t\tlogging.Debug(logCtx, \"wingman auto-apply skip: already in apply subprocess\")\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\treviewPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)\n\tif _, statErr := os.Stat(reviewPath); statErr != nil {\n\t\tlogging.Debug(logCtx, \"wingman auto-apply skip: no REVIEW.md pending\")\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\twingmanState := loadWingmanStateDirect(repoRoot)\n\tif wingmanState != nil && wingmanState.ApplyAttemptedAt != nil {\n\t\tlogging.Debug(logCtx, \"wingman auto-apply already attempted, skipping\",\n\t\t\tslog.Time(\"attempted_at\", *wingmanState.ApplyAttemptedAt),\n\t\t)\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\t// Don't spawn background auto-apply if a live session exists.\n\t// The prompt-submit hook will inject REVIEW.md as additionalContext,\n\t// which is visible to the user in their terminal.\n\tif hasAnyLiveSession(repoRoot) {\n\t\tlogging.Debug(logCtx, \"wingman auto-apply deferred: live session will handle via injection\")\n\t\tfmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, \"[wingman] Review pending — will be injected on next prompt\\n\")\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tfmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, \"[wingman] Pending review found, spawning auto-apply (no live sessions)\\n\")\n\tlogging.Info(logCtx, \"wingman auto-apply spawning (no live sessions)\",\n\t\tslog.String(\"review_path\", reviewPath),\n\t)\n\tspawnDetachedWingmanApply(repoRoot)\n}\n\n// outputWingmanStopNotification outputs a systemMessage notification about\n// wingman status at the end of a stop hook. This makes wingman activity visible\n// in the agent terminal without injecting context into the agent's conversation.\n// Best-effort: status may be stale due to concurrent wingman processes.\nfunc outputWingmanStopNotification(repoRoot string) {\n\tif !settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tif os.Getenv(\"ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY\") != \"\" {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\tlockPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanLockFile)\n\tif info, err := os.Stat(lockPath); err == nil && time.Since(info.ModTime()) <= wingmanNotificationLockThreshold {\n\t\t_ = outputHookMessage(\"[Wingman] Reviewing your changes...\") //nolint:errcheck // best-effort notification\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\treviewPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)\n\tif _, err := os.Stat(reviewPath); err == nil {\n\t\t_ = outputHookMessage(\"[Wingman] Review pending \\u2014 will be addressed on your next prompt\") //nolint:errcheck // best-effort notification\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n}\n"
}

   471→func runWingmanApply(repoRoot string) error {
   472→	wingmanLog("apply process started (pid=%d)", os.Getpid())
   473→
   474→	reviewPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)
   475→	if !fileExists(reviewPath) {
   476→		wingmanLog("no REVIEW.md found at %s, nothing to apply", reviewPath)
   477→		return nil
   478→	}
   479→	wingmanLog("REVIEW.md found at %s", reviewPath)
   480→
   481→	// Retry prevention: check if apply was already attempted for this review
   482→	state := loadWingmanStateDirect(repoRoot)
   483→	switch {
   484→	case state == nil:
   485→		wingmanLog("no wingman state found, proceeding without session check")
   486→	case state.ApplyAttemptedAt != nil:
   487→		wingmanLog("apply already attempted at %s, skipping", state.ApplyAttemptedAt.Format(time.RFC3339))
   488→		return nil
   489→	default:
   490→		wingmanLog("wingman state loaded: session=%s", state.SessionID)
   491→	}
   492→
   493→	// Re-check session hasn't become active (user may have typed during spawn delay).
   494→	// IDLE and ENDED are safe — only ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED should block.
   495→	if state != nil && state.SessionID != "" {
   496→		sessDir := findSessionStateDir(repoRoot)
   497→		if sessDir != "" {
   498→			phaseInfo := readSessionPhaseInfo(sessDir, state.SessionID)
   499→			if phaseInfo.Phase != "" && session.Phase(phaseInfo.Phase).IsActive() {
   500→				wingmanLog("session is active (phase=%s), aborting (next stop hook will retry)", phaseInfo.Phase)
   501→				return nil
   502→			}
   503→			wingmanLog("session phase=%s, safe to proceed", phaseInfo.Phase)
   504→		}
   505→	}
   506→
   507→	// Mark apply as attempted BEFORE triggering
   508→	if state != nil {
   509→		now := time.Now()
   510→		state.ApplyAttemptedAt = &now
   511→		saveWingmanStateDirect(repoRoot, state)
   512→	}
   513→
   514→	wingmanLog("triggering auto-apply via claude --continue")
   515→	applyStart := time.Now()
   516→	if err := triggerAutoApply(repoRoot); err != nil {
   517→		wingmanLog("ERROR auto-apply failed after %s: %v", time.Since(applyStart).Round(time.Millisecond), err)
   518→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to trigger auto-apply: %w", err)
   519→	}
   520→	wingmanLog("auto-apply completed in %s", time.Since(applyStart).Round(time.Millisecond))
   521→
   522→	return nil
   523→}

   525→// triggerAutoApply spawns claude --continue to apply the review suggestions.
   526→func triggerAutoApply(repoRoot string) error {
   527→	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), wingmanApplyTimeout)
   528→	defer cancel()
   529→
   530→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "claude",
   531→		"--continue",
   532→		"--print",
   533→		"--setting-sources", "",
   534→		// Auto-accept edits so the agent can modify files and delete REVIEW.md
   535→		// without requiring user consent (this runs in a background process).
   536→		"--permission-mode", "acceptEdits",
   537→		wingmanApplyInstruction,

   541→	// ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY=1 so git hooks (post-commit) know not to
   542→	// trigger another wingman review (prevents infinite recursion).
   543→	env := wingmanStripGitEnv(os.Environ())

   121→		allFiles = append(allFiles, f+" (modified)")
   122→	}
   123→	for _, f := range payload.NewFiles {
   124→		allFiles = append(allFiles, f+" (new)")
   125→	}
   126→	for _, f := range payload.DeletedFiles {

   131→	// Read session context from checkpoint data (best-effort)
   132→	sessionContext := readSessionContext(repoRoot, payload.SessionID)
   133→	if sessionContext != "" {
   134→		wingmanLog("session context loaded: %d bytes", len(sessionContext))
   135→	}

   139→	wingmanLog("review prompt built: %d bytes", len(prompt))

   141→	// Call Claude CLI for review
   142→	wingmanLog("calling claude CLI (model=%s, timeout=%s)", wingmanReviewModel, wingmanReviewTimeout)
   143→	reviewStart := time.Now()
   144→	reviewText, err := callClaudeForReview(repoRoot, prompt)

   147→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get review from Claude: %w", err)

   149→	wingmanLog("review received: %d bytes in %s", len(reviewText), time.Since(reviewStart).Round(time.Millisecond))

   153→	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(reviewPath), 0o750); err != nil {
   154→		wingmanLog("ERROR creating directory: %v", err)
   155→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create directory: %w", err)
   156→	}

   163→
   164→	// Update dedup state — write directly to known path instead of using
   165→	// os.Chdir (which mutates process-wide state).
   166→	allFilePaths := make([]string, 0, len(payload.ModifiedFiles)+len(payload.NewFiles)+len(payload.DeletedFiles))
   167→	allFilePaths = append(allFilePaths, payload.ModifiedFiles...)
   168→	allFilePaths = append(allFilePaths, payload.NewFiles...)
   169→	allFilePaths = append(allFilePaths, payload.DeletedFiles...)
   170→
   171→	saveWingmanStateDirect(repoRoot, &WingmanState{
   172→		SessionID:     payload.SessionID,
   173→		FilesHash:     computeFilesHash(allFilePaths),
   174→		ReviewedAt:    time.Now(),
   175→		ReviewApplied: false,
   176→	})

   179→	// If any session is live (IDLE/ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED), don't auto-apply
   180→	// in the background. The prompt-submit hook will inject REVIEW.md as
   181→	// additionalContext when the user sends their next prompt — this is VISIBLE
   182→	// in their terminal. Only use background auto-apply when no sessions are
   183→	// alive (e.g., user closed all sessions).
   184→	if hasAnyLiveSession(repoRoot) {

   186→		return nil
   187→	}
   188→
   189→	// No live sessions — apply in background as fallback
   190→	wingmanLog("no live sessions, triggering background auto-apply")
   191→	now := time.Now()
   192→	state := loadWingmanStateDirect(repoRoot)
   193→	if state != nil {
   194→		state.ApplyAttemptedAt = &now
   195→		saveWingmanStateDirect(repoRoot, state)

    61→**Correctness**:

    63→- Race conditions or concurrency issues

    65→

   107→// buildReviewPrompt constructs the review prompt from the payload, context, and diff.
   108→func buildReviewPrompt(prompts []string, commitMessage, sessionContext, sessionID, fileList, diff string) string {
   109→	promptText := strings.Join(prompts, "\n\n---\n\n")
   110→	if promptText == "" {
   111→		promptText = "(no prompts captured)"
   112→	}
   113→
   114→	commitMsgText := commitMessage
   115→	if commitMsgText == "" {
   116→		commitMsgText = "(no commit message)"
   117→	}
   118→
   119→	contextText := sessionContext
   120→	if contextText == "" {
   121→		contextText = "(no session context available)"
   122→	}
   123→
   124→	// Build checkpoint file paths
   125→	metadataDir := ".entire/metadata/" + sessionID
   126→	if sessionID == "" {
   127→		metadataDir = ".entire/metadata/<unknown>"
   128→	}
   129→	transcriptPath := metadataDir + "/full.jsonl"
   130→	promptPath := metadataDir + "/prompt.txt"
   131→	contextPath := metadataDir + "/context.md"
   132→
   133→	// Truncate large diffs
   134→	if len(diff) > maxDiffSize {
   135→		diff = diff[:maxDiffSize] + "\n\n... (diff truncated at 100KB)"
   136→	}
   137→
   138→	return fmt.Sprintf(reviewPromptTemplate, promptText, commitMsgText, contextText,
   139→		transcriptPath, promptPath, contextPath, fileList, diff)
   140→}
   141→

     1→// wingman_lifecycle.go contains wingman integration hooks for the lifecycle dispatcher.
     2→// These functions are called from lifecycle.go event handlers to inject wingman
     3→// review state into session start banners, turn start context, and turn end actions.
     4→package cli
     5→
     6→import (
     7→	"context"
     8→	"fmt"
     9→	"log/slog"
    10→	"os"
    11→	"path/filepath"
    12→	"time"
    13→
    14→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/logging"
    15→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/paths"
    16→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/settings"
    17→	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy"
    18→)
    19→
    20→// wingmanNotificationLockThreshold is the maximum lock file age for showing
    21→// "Reviewing your changes..." notifications. Much tighter than staleLockThreshold
    22→// (used for lock acquisition) because a real review takes at most
    23→// wingmanInitialDelay (10s) + wingmanReviewTimeout (5m) ≈ 6 minutes.
    24→// A lock older than this is almost certainly stale for notification purposes.
    25→const wingmanNotificationLockThreshold = 10 * time.Minute
    26→
    27→// appendWingmanSessionStartStatus appends wingman status to the session start banner.
    28→// Returns the message with wingman status appended.
    29→func appendWingmanSessionStartStatus(message string) string {
    30→	if !settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {
    31→		return message
    32→	}
    33→
    34→	repoRoot, rootErr := paths.RepoRoot()
    35→	if rootErr != nil {
    36→		return message + "\n  Wingman is active: your changes will be automatically reviewed."
    37→	}
    38→
    39→	if _, statErr := os.Stat(filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)); statErr == nil {
    40→		return message + "\n  Wingman: a review is pending and will be addressed on your next prompt."
    41→	}
    42→	return message + "\n  Wingman is active: your changes will be automatically reviewed."
    43→}
    44→
    45→// handleWingmanTurnStart checks for a pending wingman review and injects it
    46→// as additionalContext so the agent addresses it before the user's request.
    47→// Returns true if a hook response was written to stdout (caller should return early).
    48→func handleWingmanTurnStart(sessionID string) bool {
    49→	if !settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {
    50→		return false
    51→	}
    52→
    53→	repoRoot, rootErr := paths.RepoRoot()
    54→	if rootErr != nil {
    55→		return false
    56→	}
    57→
    58→	wingmanLogCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "wingman")
    59→
    60→	// If a review is pending, inject it as additionalContext
    61→	if _, statErr := os.Stat(filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)); statErr == nil {
    62→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Review available: .entire/REVIEW.md — injecting into context\n")
    63→		logging.Info(wingmanLogCtx, "wingman injecting review instruction on prompt-submit",
    64→			slog.String("session_id", sessionID),
    65→		)
    66→		if err := outputHookResponseWithContextAndMessage(
    67→			wingmanApplyInstruction,
    68→			"[Wingman] A code review is pending and will be addressed before your request.",
    69→		); err != nil {
    70→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Warning: failed to inject review instruction: %v\n", err)
    71→		} else {
    72→			return true // Hook response written to stdout — caller must return
    73→		}
    74→	}
    75→
    76→	// Notify if a review is currently in progress (fresh lock file).
    77→	lockPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanLockFile)
    78→	if lockInfo, statErr := os.Stat(lockPath); statErr == nil && time.Since(lockInfo.ModTime()) <= wingmanNotificationLockThreshold {
    79→		logging.Info(wingmanLogCtx, "wingman review in progress",
    80→			slog.String("session_id", sessionID),
    81→		)
    82→		if err := outputHookMessage("[Wingman] Review in progress..."); err != nil {
    83→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Warning: failed to output review-in-progress message: %v\n", err)
    84→		}
    85→	}
    86→
    87→	return false
    88→}
    89→
    90→// handleWingmanTurnEnd handles wingman actions at turn end: triggering reviews,
    91→// auto-applying pending reviews, and showing stop notifications.
    92→func handleWingmanTurnEnd(sessionID string, totalChanges int, relModifiedFiles, relNewFiles, relDeletedFiles, allPrompts []string, commitMessage string) {
    93→	repoRoot, err := paths.RepoRoot()
    94→	if err != nil {
    95→		return
    96→	}
    97→
    98→	strat := GetStrategy()
    99→
   100→	// Trigger wingman review for auto-commit strategy (commit already happened
   101→	// in SaveStep). Manual-commit triggers wingman from the git post-commit hook
   102→	// instead, since the user commits manually.
   103→	if totalChanges > 0 && strat.Name() == strategy.StrategyNameAutoCommit && settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {
   104→		triggerWingmanReview(WingmanPayload{
   105→			SessionID:     sessionID,
   106→			RepoRoot:      repoRoot,
   107→			ModifiedFiles: relModifiedFiles,
   108→			NewFiles:      relNewFiles,
   109→			DeletedFiles:  relDeletedFiles,
   110→			Prompts:       allPrompts,
   111→			CommitMessage: commitMessage,
   112→		})
   113→	}
   114→
   115→	// Auto-apply pending wingman review on turn end
   116→	triggerWingmanAutoApplyIfPending(repoRoot)
   117→
   118→	outputWingmanStopNotification(repoRoot)
   119→}
   120→
   121→// triggerWingmanAutoApplyIfPending checks for a pending REVIEW.md and spawns
   122→// the auto-apply subprocess if conditions are met. Called from the stop hook
   123→// on every turn end (both with-changes and no-changes paths).
   124→//
   125→// When a live session exists, this is a no-op: the prompt-submit injection
   126→// will deliver the review visibly in the user's terminal instead. Background
   127→// auto-apply is only used when no sessions are alive (all ended).
   128→func triggerWingmanAutoApplyIfPending(repoRoot string) {
   129→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "wingman")
   130→	if !settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {
   131→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply skip: wingman not enabled")
   132→		return
   133→	}
   134→	if os.Getenv("ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY") != "" {
   135→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply skip: already in apply subprocess")
   136→		return
   137→	}
   138→	reviewPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)
   139→	if _, statErr := os.Stat(reviewPath); statErr != nil {
   140→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply skip: no REVIEW.md pending")
   141→		return
   142→	}
   143→	wingmanState := loadWingmanStateDirect(repoRoot)
   144→	if wingmanState != nil && wingmanState.ApplyAttemptedAt != nil {
   145→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply already attempted, skipping",
   146→			slog.Time("attempted_at", *wingmanState.ApplyAttemptedAt),
   147→		)
   148→		return
   149→	}
   150→	// Don't spawn background auto-apply if a live session exists.
   151→	// The prompt-submit hook will inject REVIEW.md as additionalContext,
   152→	// which is visible to the user in their terminal.
   153→	if hasAnyLiveSession(repoRoot) {
   154→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply deferred: live session will handle via injection")
   155→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Review pending — will be injected on next prompt\n")
   156→		return
   157→	}
   158→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Pending review found, spawning auto-apply (no live sessions)\n")
   159→	logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply spawning (no live sessions)",
   160→		slog.String("review_path", reviewPath),
   161→	)
   162→	spawnDetachedWingmanApply(repoRoot)
   163→}
   164→
   165→// outputWingmanStopNotification outputs a systemMessage notification about
   166→// wingman status at the end of a stop hook. This makes wingman activity visible
   167→// in the agent terminal without injecting context into the agent's conversation.
   168→// Best-effort: status may be stale due to concurrent wingman processes.
   169→func outputWingmanStopNotification(repoRoot string) {
   170→	if !settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {
   171→		return
   172→	}
   173→	if os.Getenv("ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY") != "" {
   174→		return
   175→	}
   176→
   177→	lockPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanLockFile)
   178→	if info, err := os.Stat(lockPath); err == nil && time.Since(info.ModTime()) <= wingmanNotificationLockThreshold {
   179→		_ = outputHookMessage("[Wingman] Reviewing your changes...") //nolint:errcheck // best-effort notification
   180→		return
   181→	}
   182→
   183→	reviewPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)
   184→	if _, err := os.Stat(reviewPath); err == nil {
   185→		_ = outputHookMessage("[Wingman] Review pending \u2014 will be addressed on your next prompt") //nolint:errcheck // best-effort notification
   186→		return
   187→	}
   188→}

+// reviewHasActionableIssues reads a REVIEW.md and checks if it contains
+// actionable issue markers ([CRITICAL], [WARNING], or [SUGGESTION]).
+// Returns false if the file can't be read or contains no issues.
+func reviewHasActionableIssues(reviewPath string) bool {
+	data, err := os.ReadFile(reviewPath) //nolint:gosec // path is from repo-relative constant
+	if err != nil {
+		return false
+	}
+
+	content := string(data)
+
+	// The review format uses "### [SEVERITY] description" for each issue.
+	// Check for any of the severity markers in heading context.
+	for _, marker := range []string{"[CRITICAL]", "[WARNING]", "[SUGGESTION]"} {
+		if strings.Contains(content, marker) {
+			return true
+		}
+	}
+
+	return false

     2→
     3→# Code Review
     4→
     5→## Summary
     6→
     7→The commit accomplishes its stated goal: skip wingman REVIEW.md injection into the agent's context when the review contains no actionable issues (markers `[CRITICAL]`, `[WARNING]`, `[SUGGESTION]`). The core implementation in `wingman_lifecycle.go` is correct and well-structured. The change touches two code paths — `handleWingmanTurnStart` and `appendWingmanSessionStartStatus` — both gated by the new `reviewHasActionableIssues` function.
     8→
     9→Note: The diff is very large (100KB+) because the commit bundles many unrelated changes (agent interface refactor, new lifecycle.go file, hook preservation, CHANGELOG, README, CONTRIBUTING, E2E tests, etc.) alongside the stated wingman feature. This review focuses on the wingman changes per the commit message.
    10→
    11→## Issues
    12→
    13→### [WARNING] `triggerWingmanAutoApplyIfPending` will spawn background auto-apply for clean reviews
    14→**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/wingman_lifecycle.go:141-176`
    15→**Description:** When no live sessions exist, `triggerWingmanAutoApplyIfPending` spawns a detached `claude --continue` process to apply the REVIEW.md — even if the review has no actionable issues. This wastes API tokens and creates unnecessary background processes. The turn-start path cleans up clean reviews, but if the turn ends and no live sessions exist, the auto-apply path runs first (it's called in `handleWingmanTurnEnd` at line 129, before the next turn start ever fires).
    16→
    17→The race scenario: (1) Review completes with no actionable issues, (2) Agent turn ends, (3) `triggerWingmanAutoApplyIfPending` sees REVIEW.md exists + no live sessions → spawns auto-apply, (4) Auto-apply feeds a clean review to `claude --continue` which has nothing to fix.
    18→
    19→**Suggestion:**
    20→```go
    21→// In triggerWingmanAutoApplyIfPending, after confirming reviewPath exists:
    22→reviewPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)
    23→if _, statErr := os.Stat(reviewPath); statErr != nil {
    24→    logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply skip: no REVIEW.md pending")
    25→    return
    26→}
    27→// Skip auto-apply if the review has no actionable issues
    28→if !reviewHasActionableIssues(reviewPath) {
    29→    logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply skip: review has no actionable issues, cleaning up")
    30→    _ = os.Remove(reviewPath)
    31→    return
    32→}
    33→```
    34→
    35→### [WARNING] `outputWingmanStopNotification` shows "Review pending" for clean reviews
    36→**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/wingman_lifecycle.go:218-222`
    37→**Description:** `outputWingmanStopNotification` displays "[Wingman] Review pending — will be addressed on your next prompt" whenever REVIEW.md exists, regardless of whether it has actionable issues. This is misleading for clean reviews. Since the file persists until the next turn start or auto-apply, the user sees a pending notification that will resolve to "no issues found."
    38→
    39→**Suggestion:**
    40→```go
    41→reviewPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)
    42→if _, err := os.Stat(reviewPath); err == nil && reviewHasActionableIssues(reviewPath) {
    43→    _ = outputHookMessage("[Wingman] Review pending — will be addressed on your next prompt")
    44→    return
    45→}
    46→```
    47→
    48→### [SUGGESTION] No unit tests for `reviewHasActionableIssues`
    49→**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/wingman_lifecycle.go:181`
    50→**Description:** The `reviewHasActionableIssues` function is the core logic of this feature but has no direct unit tests. While simple, testing edge cases would be valuable: empty file, file with `[INFO]` but not actionable markers, file with marker inside a code block (currently a false positive, but documenting the expected behavior matters), and file that can't be read.
    51→
    52→**Suggestion:**
    53→Add a table-driven test like:
    54→```go
    55→func TestReviewHasActionableIssues(t *testing.T) {
    56→    tests := []struct {
    57→        name    string
    58→        content string
    59→        want    bool
    60→    }{
    61→        {"empty file", "", false},
    62→        {"clean review", "# Review\n\nNo issues found.", false},
    63→        {"critical issue", "### [CRITICAL] SQL injection\n...", true},
    64→        {"warning issue", "### [WARNING] Missing error handling\n...", true},
    65→        {"suggestion", "### [SUGGESTION] Consider adding tests\n...", true},
    66→        {"info only", "### [INFO] Good code quality\n...", false},
    67→    }
    68→    // ...
    69→}
    70→```
    71→
    72→### [SUGGESTION] `strings.Contains` matching is broad
    73→**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/wingman_lifecycle.go:191-194`
    74→**Description:** `strings.Contains(content, "[CRITICAL]")` will match the marker anywhere in the file — including in code blocks, quoted text, or even the review template instructions if they mention the format. This is unlikely to cause false positives in practice since the review is generated by the CLI's own prompt, but it's worth noting the trade-off. If tighter matching is ever needed, checking for the heading prefix `### [` would be more precise.

## Architectural Analysis: Wingman Review Integration with Agent API

Based on my thorough exploration of the codebase, here's a complete analysis of how wingman could leverage the configurable agent API:

---

### 1. CURRENT WINGMAN REVIEW IMPLEMENTATION

**File:** `/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/cmd/entire/cli/wingman_review.go`

**Current Approach (Hardcoded):**
- **Model:** Hardcoded constant `wingmanReviewModel = "opus"` (line 32)
- **Agent:** Hardcoded to invoke `claude` CLI directly via `exec.CommandContext` (line 278)
- **Command Structure:** Uses basic args to `claude`:
  ```go
  cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "claude",
      "--print",
      "--output-format", "json",
      "--model", wingmanReviewModel,    // HARDCODED: "opus"
      "--setting-sources", "",
      "--allowedTools", "Read,Glob,Grep",
      "--permission-mode", "bypassPermissions",
  )
  ```

**Key Function:** `callClaudeForReview()` (lines 272-321)
- Takes `repoRoot` and `prompt` as parameters
- Returns `(string, error)` with the review text
- Strips git environment variables to prevent hook interference
- Sets `--setting-sources ""` to disable hook callbacks (prevents recursion)
- Parses JSON response with `wingmanCLIResponse` struct

**Invocation Points:**
1. **Review triggering:** `runWingmanReview()` (lines 60-206)
   - Called from the `__review` hidden subcommand
   - Spawned as detached process from post-commit or turn-end hooks
2. **Auto-apply triggering:** `triggerAutoApply()` (lines 525-552)
   - Uses `claude --continue` to apply review suggestions
   - Also hardcoded to claude CLI

### 2. THE NEW AGENT INTERFACE ARCHITECTURE

**Location:** `/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/`

**Core Interface (`agent.go`):**
```go
type Agent interface {
    // Identity (5 methods)
    Name() AgentName
    Type() AgentType
    Description() string
    DetectPresence() (bool, error)
    ProtectedDirs() []string
    
    // Event Mapping (2 methods)
    HookNames() []string
    ParseHookEvent(hookName string, stdin io.Reader) (*Event, error)
    
    // Transcript Storage (3 methods)
    ReadTranscript(sessionRef string) ([]byte, error)
    ChunkTranscript(content []byte, maxSize int) ([][]byte, error)
    ReassembleTranscript(chunks [][]byte) ([]byte, error)
    
    // Legacy methods (8 methods)
    GetHookConfigPath() string
    SupportsHooks() bool
    ParseHookInput(hookType HookType, reader io.Reader) (*HookInput, error)
    GetSessionID(input *HookInput) string
    GetSessionDir(repoPath string) (string, error)
    ResolveSessionFile(sessionDir, agentSessionID string) string
    ReadSession(input *HookInput) (*AgentSession, error)
    WriteSession(session *AgentSession) error
    FormatResumeCommand(sessionID string) string
}
```

**Optional Interfaces:**
- `HookSupport` - For agents with lifecycle hooks (install/uninstall)
- `TranscriptAnalyzer` - For parsing transcripts to extract prompts, files, summaries
- `TranscriptPreparer` - For flushing async transcript writes before reading
- `TokenCalculator` - For computing token usage
- `SubagentAwareExtractor` - For extracting files/tokens from subagents (Tasks)

**Registered Agents:**
```go
const (
    AgentNameClaudeCode AgentName = "claude-code"
    AgentNameGemini     AgentName = "gemini"
)

const (
    AgentTypeClaudeCode AgentType = "Claude Code"
    AgentTypeGemini     AgentType = "Gemini CLI"
)
```

### 3. AGENT REGISTRY PATTERN

**Location:** `/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/registry.go`

**How Agent Discovery Works:**

```go
// Factory function pattern
type Factory func() Agent

// Global registry (thread-safe with RWMutex)
var registry = make(map[AgentName]Factory)

// Self-registration in init()
// From /Users/dip/Repositories/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/claude.go (lines 20-23)
func init() {
    agent.Register(agent.AgentNameClaudeCode, NewClaudeCodeAgent)
}

// Key Functions:
func Register(name AgentName, factory Factory)    // Register an agent
func Get(name AgentName) (Agent, error)           // Get by name
func List() []AgentName                            // List all registered agents (sorted)
func Detect() (Agent, error)                       // Auto-detect first available agent
func DetectAll() []Agent                           // Detect all available agents
func GetByAgentType(agentType AgentType) (Agent, error)  // Get by display type
func Default() Agent                               // Get default agent
```

**Claude Code Agent Implementation Example:**
- File: `/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/claude.go`
- Implements full `Agent` interface
- Registers itself at init time: `agent.Register(agent.AgentNameClaudeCode, NewClaudeCodeAgent)`
- Provides methods like:
  - `DetectPresence()` - checks for `.claude/` directory
  - `SupportsHooks()` - returns true
  - `ParseHookInput()` - decodes hook JSON from stdin
  - `GetSessionDir()` - returns Claude's session storage location

}

// Wingman config access:
func (s *EntireSettings) IsWingmanEnabled() bool {
    // Reads: s.StrategyOptions["wingman"]["enabled"]
    wingmanOpts, ok := s.StrategyOptions["wingman"].(map[string]any)
    if !ok { return false }
    enabled, ok := wingmanOpts["enabled"].(bool)
    return enabled
}

    }

### 5. HOW WINGMAN REVIEW IS TRIGGERED

**Flow:**

1. **Turn End** (`handleWingmanTurnEnd` in `wingman_lifecycle.go` lines 105-132):
   - Called from lifecycle dispatcher when agent stops
   - Auto-commit strategy: triggers review directly
   - Manual-commit: waits for git post-commit hook

2. **Git Post-Commit Hook** (`triggerWingmanFromCommit` in `wingman.go` lines 340-408):
   - Called when user commits changes
   - Extracts file list from commit via `git diff-tree`
   - Builds `WingmanPayload` struct

3. **Review Spawn** (`triggerWingmanReview` in `wingman.go` lines 252-335):
   - Performs dedup check (file hash)
   - Acquires atomic lock file to prevent concurrent reviews
   - Writes payload JSON to temp file
   - Spawns detached subprocess: `entire __review <payload-file>`

4. **Review Subprocess** (`runWingmanReview` in `wingman_review.go` lines 60-206):
   - Reads payload
   - Computes diff
   - Builds review prompt (lines 108-140 in `wingman_prompt.go`)
   - **Calls** `callClaudeForReview()` (currently hardcoded)
   - Writes `REVIEW.md` to disk
   - Optionally triggers auto-apply if no live sessions

---

### 6. WHAT THE ARCHITECTURE ENABLES

**Current Constraints:**
- Model is hardcoded to "opus"
- Agent is hardcoded to "claude" CLI
- No way to use different agents (Gemini, custom reviewers)
- No way to tune model selection (e.g., haiku for cost, sonnet for quality)

**What an Extensible Architecture Could Enable:**

**Option A: Configurable Agent Name**
```json
{
  "strategy_options": {
    "wingman": {
      "enabled": true,
      "agent": "gemini"  // Use Gemini CLI instead
    }
  }
}
```

**Option B: Configurable Model**
```json
{
  "strategy_options": {
    "wingman": {
      "enabled": true,
      "model": "sonnet"  // Override default model
    }
  }
}
```

**Option C: Full Agent Abstraction**
```json
{
  "strategy_options": {
    "wingman": {
      "enabled": true,
      "reviewer": {
        "agent": "claude-code",
        "model": "opus"  // Could be "sonnet", "haiku", etc.
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### 7. PROPOSED IMPLEMENTATION APPROACH

**What needs to change:**

#### A. **Update Wingman Settings Structure**

In `settings.go`, extend wingman options:
```go
type WingmanReviewerConfig struct {
    Enabled bool   `json:"enabled"`
    Agent   string `json:"agent,omitempty"`  // "claude-code", "gemini", etc.
    Model   string `json:"model,omitempty"`  // "opus", "sonnet", "haiku", etc.
}

// Helper to get wingman reviewer config
func (s *EntireSettings) GetWingmanReviewerConfig() *WingmanReviewerConfig {
    if s.StrategyOptions == nil {
        return nil
    }
    wingmanOpts, ok := s.StrategyOptions["wingman"].(map[string]any)
    if !ok {
        return nil
    }
    // Parse out reviewer config...
}
```

#### B. **Refactor `callClaudeForReview()` to Use Agent API**

From direct `exec.CommandContext("claude", ...)` to agent-aware invocation:

```go
func callClaudeForReview(repoRoot, prompt string) (string, error) {
    // Load wingman config with fallbacks
    s, _ := settings.Load()
    reviewerAgent := "claude-code"  // default
    reviewerModel := "opus"          // default
    
    if s != nil && s.StrategyOptions != nil {
        if wingmanCfg, ok := s.StrategyOptions["wingman"].(map[string]any); ok {
            if agent, exists := wingmanCfg["agent"].(string); exists {
                reviewerAgent = agent
            }
            if model, exists := wingmanCfg["model"].(string); exists {
                reviewerModel = model
            }
        }
    }
    
    // Get agent from registry
    ag, err := agent.Get(agent.AgentName(reviewerAgent))
    if err != nil {
        return "", fmt.Errorf("wingman reviewer agent not found: %w", err)
    }
    
    // Now what? Agent interface doesn't have "ask for review" method...
    // This is where the architecture needs thought.
}
```

#### C. **The Challenge: Agent Interface Design**

The current `Agent` interface is designed for:
- Lifecycle event parsing (hooks)
- Session management
- Transcript storage

It's **NOT** designed for:
- Making arbitrary API calls to get reviews
- Passing custom prompts and getting responses

**Two Possible Solutions:**

**Solution 1: Add Optional "Reviewer" Interface**
```go
type Reviewer interface {
    Agent
    
    // ReviewCode gets a code review for the given diff
    ReviewCode(ctx context.Context, reviewPrompt string) (string, error)
}
```

Then in `callClaudeForReview()`:
```go
ag, _ := agent.Get(reviewerAgent)
if reviewer, ok := ag.(Reviewer); ok {
    return reviewer.ReviewCode(ctx, prompt)
}
return fmt.Errorf("agent %s does not support reviews", reviewerAgent)
```

**Solution 2: Keep CLI Invocation, Just Make Model Configurable**
```go
// Simplest fix: just read model from config
func callClaudeForReview(repoRoot, prompt, reviewModel string) (string, error) {
    cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "claude",
        "--print",
        "--output-format", "json",
        "--model", reviewModel,  // CONFIGURABLE instead of hardcoded
        // ... rest of args
    )
}

// Then in runWingmanReview():
reviewerModel := "opus"  // default
if s, err := settings.Load(); err == nil && s != nil {
    if wingmanCfg, ok := s.StrategyOptions["wingman"].(map[string]any); ok {
        if model, exists := wingmanCfg["model"].(string); exists {
            reviewerModel = model
        }
    }
}
reviewText, err := callClaudeForReview(repoRoot, prompt, reviewerModel)
```

### 8. INTEGRATION POINTS IN EXISTING CODE

**Where Agent API is Already Used:**

1. **config.go (lines 65-88)** - Gets configured strategy
2. **setup.go** - Shows agent selection UI and installs hooks
3. **hook_registry.go** - Determines which agent's hooks to register
4. **debug.go** - Resolves agents for session debugging
5. **rewind.go** - Gets agent session directory for rewind operations

**Pattern: Settings → Agent Registry → Agent Instance**
```go
// Load settings
s, _ := settings.Load()

// Get agent by name from settings
ag, err := agent.Get(agent.AgentName(s.Agent))
if err != nil {
    ag = agent.Default()  // Fallback
}

// Use agent methods
if present, _ := ag.DetectPresence(); !present {
    // Handle missing agent
}
```

---

### 9. KEY ARCHITECTURAL CONSTRAINTS

**Why Wingman Can't Just Use the Current Agent Interface:**

1. **Agent Interface is Event-Based:**
   - Designed to parse lifecycle hooks from agents
   - Not designed to invoke agents with arbitrary prompts

2. **No "Ask for Review" Capability:**
   - `ParseHookEvent()` is for receiving events FROM agents
   - There's no `InvokeWithPrompt()` or similar

3. **The CLI is the Integration Point:**
   - `callClaudeForReview()` shells out to the `claude` CLI
   - Works for Claude Code (built-in `claude` command)
   - Would NOT work for Gemini (different CLI tool: `gemini` or similar)
   - Would need agent-specific invocation logic

---

### 10. RECOMMENDED PATH FORWARD

**Minimal Change (Backwards Compatible):**

1. **Add model configuration to wingman settings:**
   ```json
   {
     "strategy_options": {
       "wingman": {
         "enabled": true,
         "model": "opus"
       }
     }
   }
   ```

2. **Update `wingman_review.go`:**
   - Remove hardcoded `wingmanReviewModel = "opus"` constant
   - Load model from settings in `runWingmanReview()`
   - Pass model to `callClaudeForReview()`
   - Update `callClaudeForReview()` signature to accept model parameter

3. **Update settings helper:**
   ```go
   func (s *EntireSettings) GetWingmanModel() string {
       if s.StrategyOptions == nil {
           return "opus"  // default
       }
       wingmanOpts, ok := s.StrategyOptions["wingman"].(map[string]any)
       if !ok {
           return "opus"
       }
       model, ok := wingmanOpts["model"].(string)
       if !ok {
           return "opus"
       }
       return model
   }
   ```

4. **Update wingman enable/disable commands:**
   - Add `--model` flag to `entire wingman enable`
   - Allow CLI override: `entire wingman enable --model=sonnet`

### SUMMARY TABLE

| Aspect | Current State | New Capability (Proposed) |
|--------|---------------|--------------------------|
| **Review Model** | Hardcoded "opus" | Configurable (opus/sonnet/haiku) |
| **Review Agent** | Hardcoded "claude" CLI | Configurable per settings (future) |
| **Settings Location** | `.entire/settings.json` | Same, with new `wingman.model` field |
| **Interface Design** | Direct CLI invocation | Could extend to `Reviewer` interface |
| **Backwards Compat** | N/A | Yes - defaults to "opus" if not set |
| **Multi-Agent Support** | No (claude only) | Partial (same CLI, different model) |

This architecture shows that:

1. **Making model configurable is straightforward** - just read from settings
2. **Making agent configurable is more complex** - requires rethinking how wingman invokes reviewers
3. **The agent API exists for lifecycle management**, not for arbitrary code invocation
4. **A "Reviewer" optional interface** could bridge the gap for future multi-agent support

> AGENT

Short answer: **model is easy, agent is a bit more involved** - but both are doable.

The new Agent API is designed around lifecycle events (hooks parsing, transcript analysis), not around "invoke with a prompt." Wingman currently shells out directly to `claude --print` with hardcoded args. So the Agent API doesn't directly give us a "review this code" method.

Here's what I'd suggest:

**What's trivial today (model config):**

The model is just a hardcoded constant (`wingmanReviewModel = "opus"`). We can make it configurable via settings immediately:

```json
{
  "strategy_options": {
    "wingman": {
      "enabled": true,
      "model": "sonnet"
    }
  }
}
```

**What's a bit more work (agent config):**

Each agent has a different CLI (`claude` vs `gemini`), different flags (`--print` vs whatever Gemini uses), and different output formats. Two approaches:

1. **Quick approach** - Add agent-specific CLI invocation logic in wingman itself (a switch on agent name to build the right command). Pragmatic, works now.

2. **Clean approach** - Add an optional `Reviewer` interface to the agent package that agents can implement:
   ```go
   type Reviewer interface {
       ReviewCode(ctx context.Context, prompt string, model string) (string, error)
   }
   ```
   Claude Code implements it by shelling out to `claude --print`, Gemini implements it with `gemini` CLI, etc.

The registry pattern from the Agent API (`agent.Get("claude-code")`) and the settings pattern (`settings.Agent`) are already in place, so wiring the config is straightforward either way.

Want me to implement the model + agent configurability? I'd lean toward option 2 (the `Reviewer` interface) since it's cleaner and the plumbing already exists.

   166→func stripGitEnv(env []string) []string {

   185→		if idx := strings.LastIndex(s, "```"); idx != -1 {
   186→			s = s[:idx]

Yes, absolutely. There's already clear justification — the same "shell out to claude CLI" pattern is duplicated:

1. **Summarization** (`summarize/claude.go`) — `claude --print --model sonnet`
2. **Wingman review** (`wingman_review.go`) — `claude --print --model opus --allowedTools Read,Glob,Grep`
3. **Wingman auto-apply** (`wingman_review.go`) — `claude --continue --print --permission-mode acceptEdits`

All three duplicate the same boilerplate: `stripGitEnv`, JSON response parsing, `--setting-sources ""`, error handling. And all three are hardcoded to Claude.

A `Prompter` interface on the Agent API would consolidate this:

```go
// agent/agent.go - optional interface
type Prompter interface {
    // Prompt sends a prompt and returns the text response.
    Prompt(ctx context.Context, opts PromptOptions) (string, error)
}

type PromptOptions struct {
    Model       string   // "opus", "sonnet", etc.
    Tools       []string // allowed tools (e.g., Read, Glob, Grep)
    Permissions string   // "bypassPermissions", "acceptEdits"
    WorkDir     string   // defaults to temp dir for isolation
    Continue    bool     // continue existing session
}
```

Then Claude Code and Gemini each implement it with their own CLI invocation. Wingman and summarize both consume the same interface. Settings would specify:

```json
{
  "strategy_options": {
    "wingman": {
      "enabled": true,
      "agent": "claude-code",
      "model": "opus"
    }
  }
}
```

## Wingman Spawn Mechanism & Test Patterns - Complete Exploration

I've thoroughly examined the wingman implementation and testing patterns. Here's what I found:

### 1. **Wingman Spawn Mechanism**

#### Unix Spawn (`wingman_spawn_unix.go`)
- **`spawnDetachedWingmanReview(repoRoot, payloadPath)`**:
  - Uses `exec.CommandContext` with `syscall.SysProcAttr{Setpgid: true}` to detach from parent process group
  - Spawns: `entirely wingman __review <payloadPath>`
  - Redirects stderr to `.entire/logs/wingman.log` for background logging
  - Closes log file immediately after `Start()` so child gets independent FD
  - Calls `Process.Release()` to let process run independently
  - Non-blocking: returns immediately after `Start()`

- **`spawnDetachedWingmanApply(repoRoot)`**:
  - Similar detachment mechanism
  - Spawns: `entire wingman __apply <repoRoot>`
  - Both use `context.Background()` (not ctx with timeout) - detached processes need no deadline

#### Non-Unix Spawn (`wingman_spawn_other.go`)
- Both functions are no-ops on Windows/non-Unix platforms
- Comment explains: would need `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` + `DETACHED_PROCESS` flags (not implemented)

### 2. **Wingman Hidden Subcommands**

#### `__review` subcommand (`wingman_review.go`):
- Called by spawned process with payload file path
- **Entry point**: `newWingmanReviewCmd()` → `runWingmanReview(payloadPath)`
- **Flow**:
  1. Read + unmarshal JSON payload from file
  2. Delete payload file (cleanup immediately)
  3. Wait 10 seconds (let agent turn settle)
  4. Compute git diff (merge-base with main/master, fallback to HEAD)
  5. Build file list + read session context
  6. Call `callClaudeForReview()` with prompt
  7. Write `.entire/REVIEW.md`
  8. Save `wingman-state.json` with dedup hash
  9. **Decide auto-apply**:
     - If any live session exists (IDLE/ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED) → defer to prompt-submit injection (visible to user)
     - Otherwise → trigger background auto-apply immediately
  10. Clean up lock file (defer)

#### `__apply` subcommand:
- Called by stop hook with repoRoot as argument
- **Entry point**: `newWingmanApplyCmd()` → `runWingmanApply(repoRoot)`
- **Flow**:
  1. Check REVIEW.md exists
  2. Load wingman state, check `ApplyAttemptedAt` (prevent retry spam)
  3. **Re-check session phase** - abort if ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED (user typing)
  4. Mark apply attempted (before triggering)
  5. Spawn `claude --continue` with auto-accept edits
  6. Environment: strip GIT_* vars, set `ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY=1` (prevent recursion)

### 3. **Wingman Configuration & Enable/Disable**

#### Settings Structure (from `wingman.go`):
```go
EntireSettings.StrategyOptions = map[string]any{
    "wingman": map[string]any{
        "enabled": true/false
    }
}
```

#### Commands:
- **`entire wingman enable [--local]`**:
  - Loads merged settings (or local-only with `--local`)
  - Sets `StrategyOptions["wingman"]["enabled"] = true`
  - Saves back to project or local settings.json
  - Flag `--local` controls `settings.json` vs `settings.local.json`

- **`entire wingman disable [--local]`**:
  - Sets `enabled` to false
  - Cleans up pending `REVIEW.md` if exists
  - Same `--local` flag support

- **`entire wingman status`**:
  - Shows enabled/disabled status
  - Shows last review timestamp + status (applied/pending)
  - Lists pending REVIEW.md if exists

#### Settings Loading:
- `loadSettingsTarget(local bool)`:
  - `local=false`: Returns merged settings (`settings.json` + `settings.local.json`)
  - `local=true`: Returns only `settings.local.json` (no merge)

### 4. **Test Patterns in `wingman_test.go`**

The tests use **direct function testing** without mocking the external processes:

```go
// Test structure examples:
func TestWingmanPayload_RoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
    t.Parallel()
    // JSON serialization round-trip test
}

func TestBuildReviewPrompt_IncludesAllSections(t *testing.T) {
    t.Parallel()
    // Functional test: verify prompt composition
    // Uses string.Contains checks
}

func TestWingmanState_SaveLoad(t *testing.T) {
    // Uses t.TempDir() + t.Chdir() (NOT parallel)
    // Creates real git repo with exec.CommandContext("git", "init", tmpDir)
    // Saves/loads state files to verify persistence
}

func TestIsWingmanEnabled_Settings(t *testing.T) {
    t.Parallel()
    // Tests settings.IsWingmanEnabled() with various option maps
    // No file I/O, pure function tests
}

func TestShouldSkipPendingReview_*(t *testing.T) {
    t.Parallel()
    // Creates .entire/REVIEW.md and wingman-state.json
    // Tests stale review cleanup logic
    // Tests session ID matching
}

func TestHasAnyLiveSession_*(t *testing.T) {
    t.Parallel()
    // Creates .git/entire-sessions/*.json files
    // Tests phase detection (IDLE, ACTIVE, ACTIVE_COMMITTED, ENDED)
    // Tests staleness detection (last_interaction_time vs threshold)
}

func TestRunWingmanApply_*(t *testing.T) {
    t.Parallel()
    // Tests phase checks without spawning actual subprocess
    // Verifies ApplyAttemptedAt is/isn't set based on phase
}

func TestLoadSettingsTarget_Local(t *testing.T) {
    // Uses t.Chdir() (NOT parallel)
    // Creates real git repo + settings.json + settings.local.json
    // Tests merged vs local-only loading
}
```

**Key patterns**:
- `t.Parallel()` everywhere except tests using `t.Chdir()` or `os.Setenv()`
- Tests use `t.TempDir()` for isolated file systems
- Tests create real git repos when needed: `exec.CommandContext(context.Background(), "git", "init", tmpDir)`
- State files are simple JSON, tested with manual read/write
- Session state files checked with `os.ReadDir()` + JSON parsing
- No dependency injection for external subprocess calls (those are tested via E2E)

### 5. **Summarize Test Patterns** (`claude_test.go`)

The `CommandRunner` injection pattern shows how to test subprocess-calling code:

```go
type ClaudeGenerator struct {
    ClaudePath string
    Model string
    // Key: allow injection of exec.CommandContext
    CommandRunner func(ctx context.Context, name string, args ...string) *exec.Cmd
}

// In tests:
gen := &ClaudeGenerator{
    CommandRunner: func(ctx context.Context, _ string, _ ...string) *exec.Cmd {
        // Can return mock command or capture the cmd for inspection
        cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "sh", "-c", "printf '%s' '"+response+"'")
        capturedCmd = cmd
        return cmd
    },
}
```

**Test examples**:
- `TestClaudeGenerator_GitIsolation`: Captures cmd to verify `cmd.Dir = os.TempDir()` and GIT_* stripping
- `TestClaudeGenerator_CommandNotFound`: Returns nonexistent command to test error handling
- `TestClaudeGenerator_NonZeroExit`: Returns failing command to test exit code handling
- `TestClaudeGenerator_ValidResponse`: Returns mock JSON response to test full flow
- `TestStripGitEnv`: Direct function test of environment variable filtering
- `TestExtractJSONFromMarkdown`: Tests markdown extraction with various formats

### 6. **Key Testing Insights**

**No mocking for detached processes**:
- `callClaudeForReview()` is tested via capture + assertion on command properties
- Actual subprocess execution is tested via E2E (when explicitly requested)
- Tests verify command construction, env vars, working directory

**State management testing**:
- Session state: `.git/entire-sessions/<id>.json` files
- Wingman state: `.entire/wingman-state.json`
- Settings: `.entire/settings.json` + `.entire/settings.local.json`
- All tested via direct file I/O in tests

**Phase detection**:
- Sessions have `phase` field (string): "IDLE", "ACTIVE", "ACTIVE_COMMITTED", "ENDED"
- Tested by creating session state files with literal JSON: `{"phase":"idle"}`
- `hasAnyLiveSession()` uses `session.PhaseFromString()` to convert string → Phase enum

**Stale session detection**:
- Uses `LastInteractionTime` from JSON (not file modtime)
- Threshold: `staleActiveSessionThreshold = 4 * time.Hour`
- Only applies to ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED; IDLE always considered live

---

## Summary for Planning

The wingman implementation has these testability characteristics:

1. **Well-separated concerns**:
   - Spawn logic (platform-specific in separate files)
   - Review process (isolated in `__review` subprocess)
   - Apply process (isolated in `__apply` subprocess)
   - Settings management (through settings package)

2. **CommandRunner injection pattern** (from summarize) could be applied to wingman's `callClaudeForReview()`

3. **No test mocking needed** for detached spawning since tests just verify the triggered flow, not the actual spawned processes

4. **File-based state** makes unit testing easy without databases or complex setup

5. **Clear phase machine** in session/phase.go with enum-like behavior makes phase checking testable

    10→// Agent defines the interface for interacting with a coding agent.

    13→//
    14→// The interface is organized into four groups:
    15→//
    16→//   - Identity (5 methods): Name, Type, Description, DetectPresence, ProtectedDirs
    17→//   - Event Mapping (2 methods): HookNames, ParseHookEvent
    18→//   - Transcript Storage (3 methods): ReadTranscript, ChunkTranscript, ReassembleTranscript

    20→type Agent interface {

    26→	// Type returns the agent type identifier (e.g., "Claude Code", "Gemini CLI")

    39→	ProtectedDirs() []string

    97→// HookSupport is implemented by agents with lifecycle hooks.
    98→// This optional interface allows agents like Claude Code and Cursor to
    99→// install and manage hooks that notify Entire of agent events.
   100→type HookSupport interface {
   101→	Agent
   102→
   103→	// InstallHooks installs agent-specific hooks.
   104→	// If localDev is true, hooks point to local development build.
   105→	// If force is true, removes existing Entire hooks before installing.

   115→	// GetSupportedHooks returns the hook types this agent supports

   119→// HookHandler is implemented by agents that define their own hook vocabulary.
   120→// HookNames() is now part of the core Agent interface.
   121→// This interface is kept for backward compatibility during migration.
   122→type HookHandler interface {
   123→	Agent
   124→

   126→	GetHookNames() []string
   127→}

   129→// FileWatcher is implemented by agents that use file-based detection.
   130→// Agents like Aider that don't support hooks can use file watching
   131→// to detect session activity.
   132→type FileWatcher interface {
   133→	Agent
   134→
   135→	// GetWatchPaths returns paths to watch for session changes
   136→	GetWatchPaths() ([]string, error)
   137→
   138→	// OnFileChange handles a detected file change and returns session info
   139→	OnFileChange(path string) (*SessionChange, error)

   141→
   142→// TranscriptAnalyzer provides format-specific transcript parsing.
   143→// Agents that implement this get richer checkpoints (transcript-derived file lists,
   144→// prompts, summaries). Agents that don't still participate in the checkpoint lifecycle
   145→// via git-status-based file detection and raw transcript storage.
   146→type TranscriptAnalyzer interface {
   147→	Agent
   148→
   149→	// GetTranscriptPosition returns the current position (length) of a transcript.
   150→	// For JSONL formats (Claude Code), this is the line count.
   151→	// For JSON formats (Gemini CLI), this is the message count.
   152→	// Returns 0 if the file doesn't exist or is empty.
   153→	GetTranscriptPosition(path string) (int, error)
   154→
   155→	// ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset extracts files modified since a given offset.
   156→	// For JSONL formats (Claude Code), offset is the starting line number.
   157→	// For JSON formats (Gemini CLI), offset is the starting message index.
   158→	// Returns:
   159→	//   - files: list of file paths modified by the agent (from Write/Edit tools)
   160→	//   - currentPosition: the current position (line count or message count)
   161→	//   - error: any error encountered during reading
   162→	ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset(path string, startOffset int) (files []string, currentPosition int, err error)
   163→
   164→	// ExtractPrompts extracts user prompts from the transcript starting at the given offset.
   165→	ExtractPrompts(sessionRef string, fromOffset int) ([]string, error)
   166→
   167→	// ExtractSummary extracts a summary of the session from the transcript.
   168→	ExtractSummary(sessionRef string) (string, error)
   169→}
   170→
   171→// TranscriptPreparer is called before ReadTranscript to handle agent-specific
   172→// flush/sync requirements (e.g., Claude Code's async transcript writing).
   173→// The framework calls PrepareTranscript before ReadTranscript if implemented.
   174→type TranscriptPreparer interface {
   175→	Agent
   176→
   177→	// PrepareTranscript ensures the transcript is ready to read.
   178→	// For Claude Code, this waits for the async transcript flush to complete.
   179→	PrepareTranscript(sessionRef string) error

   181→
   182→// TokenCalculator provides token usage calculation for a session.

   184→type TokenCalculator interface {

   188→	CalculateTokenUsage(sessionRef string, fromOffset int) (*TokenUsage, error)

   193→// to ensure subagent contributions are included in checkpoints.
   194→type SubagentAwareExtractor interface {

   202→	// CalculateTotalTokenUsage computes token usage including all spawned subagents.

     1→package agent
     2→
     3→import (
     4→	"fmt"
     5→	"slices"
     6→	"sync"
     7→)
     8→
     9→var (
    10→	registryMu sync.RWMutex
    11→	registry   = make(map[AgentName]Factory)
    12→)
    13→
    14→// Factory creates a new agent instance
    15→type Factory func() Agent
    16→
    17→// Register adds an agent factory to the registry.
    18→// Called from init() in each agent implementation.
    19→func Register(name AgentName, factory Factory) {
    20→	registryMu.Lock()
    21→	defer registryMu.Unlock()
    22→	registry[name] = factory
    23→}
    24→
    25→// Get retrieves an agent by name.
    26→//
    27→
    28→func Get(name AgentName) (Agent, error) {
    29→	registryMu.RLock()
    30→	defer registryMu.RUnlock()
    31→
    32→	factory, ok := registry[name]
    33→	if !ok {
    34→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown agent: %s (available: %v)", name, List())
    35→	}
    36→	return factory(), nil
    37→}
    38→
    39→// List returns all registered agent names in sorted order.
    40→func List() []AgentName {
    41→	registryMu.RLock()
    42→	defer registryMu.RUnlock()
    43→
    44→	names := make([]AgentName, 0, len(registry))
    45→	for name := range registry {
    46→		names = append(names, name)
    47→	}
    48→	slices.Sort(names)
    49→	return names
    50→}
    51→
    52→// DetectAll returns all agents whose DetectPresence reports true.
    53→// Agents are checked in sorted name order (via List()) for deterministic results.
    54→// Returns an empty slice when no agent is detected.
    55→func DetectAll() []Agent {
    56→	names := List() // sorted, lock-safe
    57→
    58→	var detected []Agent
    59→	for _, name := range names {
    60→		ag, err := Get(name)
    61→		if err != nil {
    62→			continue
    63→		}
    64→		if present, err := ag.DetectPresence(); err == nil && present {
    65→			detected = append(detected, ag)
    66→		}
    67→	}
    68→	return detected
    69→}
    70→
    71→// Detect attempts to auto-detect which agent is being used.
    72→// Iterates registered agents in sorted name order for deterministic results.
    73→// Returns the first agent whose DetectPresence reports true.
    74→func Detect() (Agent, error) {
    75→	detected := DetectAll()
    76→	if len(detected) == 0 {
    77→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("no agent detected (available: %v)", List())
    78→	}
    79→	return detected[0], nil
    80→}
    81→
    82→// AgentName is the registry key type for agents (e.g., "claude-code", "gemini").
    83→//
    84→//nolint:revive // stuttering is intentional - distinguishes from AgentType when both are used
    85→type AgentName string
    86→
    87→// AgentType is the display name type stored in metadata/trailers (e.g., "Claude Code", "Gemini CLI").
    88→//
    89→//nolint:revive // stuttering is intentional - distinguishes from AgentName when both are used
    90→type AgentType string
    91→
    92→// Agent name constants (registry keys)
    93→const (
    94→	AgentNameClaudeCode AgentName = "claude-code"
    95→	AgentNameGemini     AgentName = "gemini"
    96→)
    97→
    98→// Agent type constants (type identifiers stored in metadata/trailers)
    99→const (
   100→	AgentTypeClaudeCode AgentType = "Claude Code"
   101→	AgentTypeGemini     AgentType = "Gemini CLI"
   102→	AgentTypeUnknown    AgentType = "Agent" // Fallback for backwards compatibility
   103→)
   104→
   105→// DefaultAgentName is the registry key for the default agent.
   106→const DefaultAgentName AgentName = AgentNameClaudeCode
   107→
   108→// GetByAgentType retrieves an agent by its type identifier.
   109→//
   110→// Note: This uses a linear search that instantiates agents until a match is found.
   111→// This is acceptable because:
   112→//   - Agent count is small (~2-20 agents)
   113→//   - Agent factories are lightweight (empty struct allocation)
   114→//   - Called infrequently (commit hooks, rewind, debug commands - not hot paths)
   115→//   - Cost is ~400ns worst case vs milliseconds for I/O operations
   116→//
   117→// Only optimize if agent count exceeds 100 or profiling shows this as a bottleneck.
   118→func GetByAgentType(agentType AgentType) (Agent, error) {
   119→	registryMu.RLock()
   120→	defer registryMu.RUnlock()
   121→
   122→	for _, factory := range registry {
   123→		ag := factory()
   124→		if ag.Type() == agentType {
   125→			return ag, nil
   126→		}
   127→	}
   128→
   129→	return nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown agent type: %s", agentType)
   130→}
   131→
   132→// AllProtectedDirs returns the union of ProtectedDirs from all registered agents.
   133→func AllProtectedDirs() []string {
   134→	// Copy factories under the lock, then release before calling external code.
   135→	registryMu.RLock()
   136→	factories := make([]Factory, 0, len(registry))
   137→	for _, f := range registry {
   138→		factories = append(factories, f)
   139→	}
   140→	registryMu.RUnlock()
   141→
   142→	seen := make(map[string]struct{})
   143→	var dirs []string
   144→	for _, factory := range factories {
   145→		for _, d := range factory().ProtectedDirs() {
   146→			if _, ok := seen[d]; !ok {
   147→				seen[d] = struct{}{}
   148→				dirs = append(dirs, d)
   149→			}
   150→		}
   151→	}
   152→	slices.Sort(dirs)
   153→	return dirs
   154→}
   155→
   156→// Default returns the default agent.
   157→// Returns nil if the default agent is not registered.
   158→//
   159→//nolint:errcheck // Factory pattern returns interface; error is acceptable to ignore for default
   160→func Default() Agent {
   161→	a, _ := Get(DefaultAgentName)
   162→	return a
   163→}
