   541→// shouldSkipPendingReview checks whether a pending REVIEW.md should prevent
   542→// a new review from being triggered. It cleans up stale/orphaned reviews.
   543→//
   544→// Returns true only when REVIEW.md exists AND belongs to the current session
   545→// AND is younger than wingmanStaleReviewTTL.
   546→func shouldSkipPendingReview(repoRoot, currentSessionID string) bool {
   547→	reviewPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)
   548→	if _, err := os.Stat(reviewPath); err != nil {
   549→		return false // No REVIEW.md, don't skip
   550→	}
   551→
   552→	// REVIEW.md exists — check state to determine if it's current or stale
   553→	state := loadWingmanStateDirect(repoRoot)
   554→	if state == nil {
   555→		// Orphan: REVIEW.md without state file — clean up
   556→		_ = os.Remove(reviewPath)
   557→		return false
   558→	}
   559→
   560→	if state.SessionID != currentSessionID {
   561→		// Different session — stale review, clean up
   562→		_ = os.Remove(reviewPath)
   563→		return false
   564→	}
   565→
   566→	if time.Since(state.ReviewedAt) > wingmanStaleReviewTTL {
   567→		// Same session but too old — clean up
   568→		_ = os.Remove(reviewPath)
   569→		return false
   570→	}
   571→
   572→	return true // Current session, fresh review — skip
   573→}

   574→func TestLoadSettingsTarget_Local(t *testing.T) {
   575→	// Uses t.Chdir so cannot be parallel
   576→	tmpDir := t.TempDir()
   577→
   578→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(context.Background(), "git", "init", tmpDir)
   579→	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
   580→		t.Fatalf("failed to git init: %v", err)
   581→	}
   582→
   583→	entireDir := filepath.Join(tmpDir, ".entire")
   584→	if err := os.MkdirAll(entireDir, 0o755); err != nil {
   585→		t.Fatal(err)
   586→	}
   587→
   588→	// Write project settings with wingman disabled
   589→	projectSettings := `{"strategy": "manual-commit", "enabled": true, "strategy_options": {"wingman": {"enabled": false}}}`
   590→	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(entireDir, "settings.json"), []byte(projectSettings), 0o644); err != nil {
   591→		t.Fatal(err)
   592→	}
   593→
   594→	// Write local settings with different strategy
   595→	localSettings := `{"strategy": "` + strategyDisplayAutoCommit + `"}`
   596→	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(entireDir, "settings.local.json"), []byte(localSettings), 0o644); err != nil {
   597→		t.Fatal(err)
   598→	}
   599→
   600→	t.Chdir(tmpDir)
   601→
   602→	t.Run("local=false returns merged settings", func(t *testing.T) {
   603→		s, err := loadSettingsTarget(false)
   604→		if err != nil {
   605→			t.Fatalf("unexpected error: %v", err)
   606→		}
   607→		// Merged: local overrides project strategy
   608→		if s.Strategy != strategyDisplayAutoCommit {
   609→			t.Errorf("Strategy = %q, want %q", s.Strategy, strategyDisplayAutoCommit)
   610→		}
   611→	})
   612→
   613→	t.Run("local=true returns only local settings", func(t *testing.T) {
   614→		s, err := loadSettingsTarget(true)
   615→		if err != nil {
   616→			t.Fatalf("unexpected error: %v", err)
   617→		}
   618→		if s.Strategy != strategyDisplayAutoCommit {
   619→			t.Errorf("Strategy = %q, want %q", s.Strategy, strategyDisplayAutoCommit)
   620→		}
   621→		// Local file has no wingman settings
   622→		if s.IsWingmanEnabled() {
   623→			t.Error("local settings should not have wingman enabled")
   624→		}
   625→	})
   626→}

   785→func TestHasAnyLiveSession_RecentModtimeButStaleInteraction(t *testing.T) {

   788→	tmpDir := t.TempDir()

   801→	if err := os.WriteFile(sessFile, []byte(sessData), 0o644); err != nil {

   806→	if hasAnyLiveSession(tmpDir) {

   811→func TestRunWingmanApply_EndedPhaseProceeds(t *testing.T) {
   812→	t.Parallel()
   813→
   814→	// This test verifies that runWingmanApply does NOT abort when the session
   815→	// phase is ENDED (the bug fix). We can't test the full auto-apply (it
   816→	// spawns claude CLI), but we can verify it passes the phase check.
   817→	tmpDir := t.TempDir()
   818→	entireDir := filepath.Join(tmpDir, ".entire")
   819→	if err := os.MkdirAll(entireDir, 0o755); err != nil {
   820→		t.Fatal(err)
   821→	}
   822→
   823→	// Create REVIEW.md
   824→	reviewPath := filepath.Join(entireDir, "REVIEW.md")
   825→	if err := os.WriteFile(reviewPath, []byte("review content"), 0o644); err != nil {
   826→		t.Fatal(err)
   827→	}
   828→
   829→	// Create wingman state
   830→	saveWingmanStateDirect(tmpDir, &WingmanState{
   831→		SessionID:  "sess-ended",
   832→		FilesHash:  "hash1",
   833→		ReviewedAt: time.Now(),
   834→	})
   835→
   836→	// Create session state dir with ENDED phase
   837→	sessDir := filepath.Join(tmpDir, ".git", "entire-sessions")
   838→	if err := os.MkdirAll(sessDir, 0o755); err != nil {
   839→		t.Fatal(err)
   840→	}
   841→	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(sessDir, "sess-ended.json"), []byte(`{"phase":"ended"}`), 0o644); err != nil {
   842→		t.Fatal(err)
   843→	}
   844→
   845→	// runWingmanApply will pass the phase check but fail at triggerAutoApply
   846→	// (no claude CLI). The important thing is it doesn't return nil early
   847→	// with "session became active" — it should get past the phase check.
   848→	err := runWingmanApply(tmpDir)
   849→	if err == nil {
   850→		t.Log("runWingmanApply returned nil (auto-apply succeeded or no claude CLI)")
   851→	} else {
   852→		// Expected: fails at triggerAutoApply because claude CLI isn't available
   853→		if strings.Contains(err.Error(), "session became active") {
   854→			t.Error("should not abort with 'session became active' for ENDED phase")
   855→		}
   856→		t.Logf("runWingmanApply failed as expected (no claude CLI): %v", err)
   857→	}
   858→
   859→	// Verify apply was attempted (state should be updated)
   860→	state := loadWingmanStateDirect(tmpDir)
   861→	if state == nil {
   862→		t.Fatal("expected wingman state to exist")
   863→	}
   864→	if state.ApplyAttemptedAt == nil {
   865→		t.Error("ApplyAttemptedAt should be set after passing phase check")
   866→	}
   867→}

> AGENT

OK so `nolintlint` is enabled with `require-explanation: true` and `require-specific: true`. With `fix: true`, the nolintlint fixer will REMOVE any nolint directives it considers unused. But the ireturn fixer can't actually fix the issue (it's a design choice), so it gets stuck in a loop.

The real issue: when `--fix` runs, `nolintlint` thinks the `//nolint:ireturn` is "unused" (because `ireturn` was already auto-fixed or suppressed), so it removes the directive. Then on the next pass, ireturn finds the issue again.

The proper approach is to use the `ireturn.allow` list instead. Let me check if I can add `Generator` to the allow list, or better yet, just look at how this function was originally written before our changes.

**`cmd/entire/cli/wingman.go`** — `newWingmanEnableCmd()` now has:
- `--agent` flag — specify agent by name (e.g., `--agent claude-code`)
- `--model` flag — specify model (e.g., `--model sonnet`)
- Interactive picker when no flags given: detects agents implementing `Prompter`, shows a `huh.NewSelect` for agent and model
- Non-interactive fallback (no TTY): uses defaults silently
- Validation: rejects unknown agents and agents that don't implement `Prompter`

**`newWingmanStatusCmd()`** now shows:
```
Wingman: enabled
Agent: claude-code
Model: opus
```

**Helper functions added:**
- `resolveWingmanEnableAgent()` — validates flag or shows picker
- `resolveWingmanEnableModel()` — validates flag or shows picker
- `findPrompterAgents()` — filters registry to Prompter-implementing agents

**`cmd/entire/cli/wingman_test.go`** — 8 new tests covering flag validation, non-interactive defaults, and settings persistence.

**`.golangci.yaml`** — Added `summarize.Generator` to `ireturn.allow` list (replaces fragile nolint directive that `fix: true` mode kept stripping).

**Review addressed:** Fixed the shell injection concern in `prompter_test.go` — inlined the JSON response directly in the printf command instead of concatenating a variable into a shell string. The other review items were about pre-existing code outside this PR's scope (hook parsing, dead structs, interface docs).

---

Now to your question: you're asking if, after the wingman review completes, we could automatically prompt the main agent session (e.g., Claude Code) to address the review without the user having to type anything — essentially a 20-second timeout that auto-triggers a prompt.

The short answer is **no, not with the current architecture**. Here's why:

1. **Claude Code has no external prompt injection API** — there's no way to programmatically send a message into a running Claude Code session from outside. The `--continue` flag starts a *new* subprocess that continues the conversation, but it can't poke a live session.

2. **The current auto-apply flow** (`triggerAutoApply`) already uses `claude --continue` — but it runs as a *separate detached process*, not inside the user's interactive session. It works, but the user doesn't see it happening in their terminal.

3. **What IS possible today:** The stop hook (`handleWingmanTurnEnd`) already triggers auto-apply when a review is pending. The `SessionStart` hook injects the review as `additionalContext` on the next prompt. So the review *does* get surfaced automatically — just on the next user interaction.

To get true "auto-prompt after 20s of idle", you'd need either:
- A Claude Code plugin/MCP extension that can inject prompts into a running session (doesn't exist)
- A terminal automation approach (sending keystrokes to the terminal — fragile and platform-specific)
- Changes to Claude Code itself to support an external trigger mechanism

The closest feasible approach would be making the auto-apply (`claude --continue`) more aggressive — reducing its trigger conditions so it fires sooner. But it still runs as a separate process, not in the user's visible session.

## Ralph Wiggum: Autonomous AI Loops

The Ralph technique is a simple while loop that repeatedly feeds an AI agent a prompt until completion. Named after The Simpsons character, it embodies the philosophy of persistent iteration despite setbacks.

### How It Works

Claude Code receives a task, works on it, and when it tries to exit, a Stop hook blocks the exit and feeds the same prompt back in. The files it just changed are still there, so each iteration can build on the last one.

### Key Features

Ralph features an autonomous development loop with dual-condition exit detection, session continuity across iterations, configurable timeouts, and rate limiting. It enables continuous autonomous development cycles where Claude Code iteratively improves your project until completion, with built-in safeguards to prevent infinite loops and API overuse.

### Usage

You start an iterative session with `/ralph-loop "your prompt here" --max-iterations 10 --completion-promise "DONE"`. The loop continues until Claude outputs the completion promise or reaches the iteration limit.

### Real-World Results

Geoffrey Huntley ran a 3-month loop that built a complete programming language. YC hackathon teams shipped 6+ repos overnight for $297 in API costs.

### When to Use

The technique shines for batch operations: large refactors, support ticket triage, test coverage, documentation.

# Ralph Wiggum Plugin Overview

The Ralph Wiggum plugin implements an iterative AI development loop for Claude Code. Here's how it works:

## Core Mechanism

**Ralph is a self-referential feedback loop** that uses a **Stop hook** to intercept Claude's exit attempts and re-prompt with the same task:

```bash
# You run ONCE:
/ralph-loop "Your task description" --completion-promise "DONE"

# Then Claude Code automatically:
# 1. Works on the task
# 2. Tries to exit
# 3. Stop hook blocks exit
# 4. Stop hook feeds the SAME prompt back
# 5. Repeat until completion
```

## How It Works

The loop operates **inside your current session** (no external bash loops needed). The key features:

- **The prompt never changes** between iterations
- Claude's **previous work persists in files**
- Each iteration sees **modified files and git history**
- Claude **autonomously improves** by reading its own past work
- Loop continues until the **completion promise is output**

## Commands

### `/ralph-loop`
```bash
/ralph-loop "<prompt>" --max-iterations <n> --completion-promise "<text>"
```

**Options:**
- `--max-iterations <n>` - Stop after N iterations (default: unlimited)
- `--completion-promise <text>` - Phrase that signals completion

### `/cancel-ralph`
Cancels the active Ralph loop.

## Example Usage

```bash
/ralph-loop "Build a REST API for todos. Requirements: CRUD operations, input validation, tests. Output <promise>COMPLETE</promise> when done." --completion-promise "COMPLETE" --max-iterations 50
```

Claude will iteratively:
1. Implement the API
2. Run tests and see failures
3. Fix bugs based on test output
4. Iterate until all requirements met

## Philosophy

- **Iteration > Perfection**: Don't aim for perfect on first try
- **Failures Are Data**: Use predictable failures to tune prompts
- **Operator Skill Matters**: Success depends on writing good prompts
- **Persistence Wins**: The loop handles retry logic automatically

## Best Practices

✅ **Clear completion criteria** with testable conditions
✅ **Incremental goals** broken into phases
✅ **Self-correction** via TDD (write tests → implement → verify → fix)
✅ **Escape hatches** using `--max-iterations` as safety net

The plugin is ideal for well-defined, iterative tasks with automatic verification (tests, linters) where you can walk away and let the loop refine the work.

Yeah, you've nailed the fundamental problem. The Stop hook is the only re-entry point, so you'd end up with a polling loop:

```
Agent finishes → Stop hook fires → review not ready → re-prompt "wait"
→ agent says "ok" → Stop hook fires → review still not ready → re-prompt "wait"
→ ... (burning API calls for minutes)
→ review lands → inject it
```

That's expensive and ugly. A few alternatives worth considering:

**1. Stop hook with a blocking wait** — instead of re-prompting, the hook script itself sleeps and polls for REVIEW.md for up to N seconds before returning. Claude Code stays in the "stopping" state, no extra API calls. Downside: the session looks frozen to the user for however long the review takes (could be minutes).

**2. Short-window opportunistic** — the Stop hook waits ~15-20 seconds (the review has a 10s initial delay already). If the review lands within that window, inject it immediately. If not, let the session end normally — the review gets picked up on the next `UserPromptSubmit` as it does today. This catches fast reviews without the polling cost.

**3. Accept the current UX** — the review already gets injected on the next prompt via `UserPromptSubmit`. The latency is "however long until the user types next," which in practice is often seconds. The only scenario where auto-prompt helps is if the user walks away.

Option 2 feels like the best balance — a short blocking wait in the Stop hook that catches most reviews without wasting API calls or freezing the session for minutes. But it's a bet on review speed.

## Comprehensive Analysis of the Stop Hook, Wingman Integration, and Auto-Loop Mechanics

Based on my thorough examination of the codebase, here are the detailed answers to your questions:

### 1. **Stop Hook Handler - Complete Flow**

**File**: `/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/hooks.go` (lines 41-42)

The Stop hook is parsed in `parseTurnEnd()`:
```go
func (c *ClaudeCodeAgent) parseTurnEnd(stdin io.Reader) (*agent.Event, error) {
	raw, err := agent.ReadAndParseHookInput[sessionInfoRaw](stdin)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return &agent.Event{
		Type:       agent.TurnEnd,
		SessionID:  raw.SessionID,
		SessionRef: raw.TranscriptPath,
		Timestamp:  time.Now(),
	}, nil
}
```

**Called from**: `/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go` line 44-45 in `DispatchLifecycleEvent()`, which routes to `handleLifecycleTurnEnd()`.

**Handler**: `/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go` lines 160-429 in `handleLifecycleTurnEnd()`.

**Key action**: Line 422 calls `handleWingmanTurnEnd()` which is the wingman integration point.

### 2. **Wingman Turn End Handler - The Critical Code**

**File**: `/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/cmd/entire/cli/wingman_lifecycle.go` lines 103-132

```go
// handleWingmanTurnEnd handles wingman actions at turn end: triggering reviews,
// auto-applying pending reviews, and showing stop notifications.
func handleWingmanTurnEnd(sessionID string, totalChanges int, relModifiedFiles, relNewFiles, relDeletedFiles, allPrompts []string, commitMessage string) {
	repoRoot, err := paths.RepoRoot()
	if err != nil {
		return
	}

	strat := GetStrategy()

	// Trigger wingman review for auto-commit strategy (commit already happened
	// in SaveStep). Manual-commit triggers wingman from the git post-commit hook
	// instead, since the user commits manually.
	if totalChanges > 0 && strat.Name() == strategy.StrategyNameAutoCommit && settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {
		triggerWingmanReview(WingmanPayload{
			SessionID:     sessionID,
			RepoRoot:      repoRoot,
			ModifiedFiles: relModifiedFiles,
			NewFiles:      relNewFiles,
			DeletedFiles:  relDeletedFiles,
			Prompts:       allPrompts,
			CommitMessage: commitMessage,
		})
	}

	// Auto-apply pending wingman review on turn end
	triggerWingmanAutoApplyIfPending(repoRoot)

	outputWingmanStopNotification(repoRoot)
}
```

**Key point**: The Stop hook does NOT return a hook response directly. It only outputs notifications via `outputWingmanStopNotification()` which uses `outputHookMessage()` (line 220 of wingman_lifecycle.go):

```go
_ = outputHookMessage("[Wingman] Reviewing your changes...") //nolint:errcheck
```

### 3. **Hook Response Format - How Hooks Can Inject Context**

**File**: `/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/cmd/entire/cli/hooks.go` lines 235-294

The hook response has **three possible mechanisms**:

```go
type hookSpecificOutput struct {
	HookEventName     string `json:"hookEventName"`
	AdditionalContext string `json:"additionalContext,omitempty"`
}

type hookResponse struct {
	SystemMessage      string              `json:"systemMessage,omitempty"`
	HookSpecificOutput *hookSpecificOutput `json:"hookSpecificOutput,omitempty"`
}
```

**Three output functions exist**:

1. **`outputHookResponse()` (line 253-264)** - SessionStart hook format:
   - Injects `additionalContext` into the agent's conversation
   - Has both systemMessage and hookSpecificOutput

2. **`outputHookMessage()` (line 271-277)** - Information-only:
   - Only outputs `systemMessage` - shown to user but NOT injected into agent
   - Used for notifications

3. **`outputHookResponseWithContextAndMessage()` (line 282-294)** - UserPromptSubmit (wingman review injection):
   ```go
   resp := hookResponse{
       SystemMessage: message,
       HookSpecificOutput: &hookSpecificOutput{
           HookEventName:     "UserPromptSubmit",
           AdditionalContext: additionalContext,
       },
   }
   ```

**Key insight**: Only `UserPromptSubmit` and `SessionStart` hooks can inject `additionalContext`. The Stop hook **CANNOT** inject context to trigger a new turn.

### 4. **Current Wingman Auto-Apply Flow - NO Auto-Loop via Hooks**

**File**: `/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/cmd/entire/cli/wingman_review.go` lines 476-531

The **Stop hook does NOT return a next prompt**. Instead, the Stop hook invokes `triggerWingmanAutoApplyIfPending()` (wingman_lifecycle.go line 129) which:

1. **Checks preconditions** (lines 142-161):
   - Wingman enabled
   - Not already in ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY subprocess
   - REVIEW.md exists
   - Review has actionable issues
   - No live session exists

2. **If conditions met**: Spawns a **detached subprocess** via `spawnDetachedWingmanApply()` that runs:
   ```bash
   entire wingman __apply <repo-root>
   ```

3. **The `__apply` subcommand** (wingman_review.go lines 476-531) then calls `triggerAutoApply()` which invokes:
   ```bash
   claude --continue --print --permission-mode acceptEdits <wingman-instruction>
   ```

**Critical**: This is NOT a hook-based loop. It's a **background subprocess** that:
- Sets `ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY=1` env var to prevent recursion
- Runs as a separate Claude Code process
- Does NOT re-inject into the current session via hooks

### 5. **Session Phase and Stop Hook Timing**

**File**: `/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/cmd/entire/cli/session/phase.go` lines 155-190

The Stop hook fires when a turn ends:

1. **Phase transitions** (via `lifecycle.go` line 419):
   ```go
   transitionSessionTurnEnd(sessionID)  // ACTIVE → IDLE
   ```

2. **State machine: `EventTurnEnd`** (phase.go lines 200-204):
   ```go
   case EventTurnEnd:
       return TransitionResult{
           NewPhase: PhaseIdle,
           Actions:  []Action{ActionUpdateLastInteraction},
       }
   ```

3. **Sequence**:
   - Agent finishes turn → `handleLifecycleTurnEnd()` called
   - Checkpoint saved via `strat.SaveStep()`
   - Phase transitions from ACTIVE → IDLE
   - `handleWingmanTurnEnd()` called
   - Stop hook fires (outside of state machine)

**State at stop hook**: Session is now in **IDLE** phase (line 419 of lifecycle.go shows transition happens before wingman handlers).

### 6. **Hook Timeout - NOT Configurable at Framework Level**

**File**: `/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/cmd/entire/cli/wingman_review.go` lines 28-45

Hook timeouts are **agent-specific**, not configurable via framework:

```go
const (
	wingmanInitialDelay = 10 * time.Second
	wingmanReviewTimeout = 5 * time.Minute    // Review timeout (not for Stop hook)
	wingmanApplyTimeout = 15 * time.Minute    // Apply timeout
)
```

**Critical finding**: The **Stop hook itself has NO timeout**. However:
- The Stop hook output functions are synchronous (write JSON to stdout)
- Any long-running work in Stop hook would block the agent
- **The Stop hook CANNOT call blocking operations without timing out Claude Code**

**The workaround**: Use detached subprocesses (like `spawnDetachedWingmanApply()`) so the hook returns immediately while async work continues.

### 7. **Complete Wingman Review + Apply Call Chain**

```
Stop Hook (fire)
  ├─ handleWingmanTurnEnd()
  │   ├─ triggerWingmanReview()  [async spawn, returns immediately]
  │   ├─ triggerWingmanAutoApplyIfPending()
  │   │   └─ hasAnyLiveSession()? 
  │   │       ├─ YES → skip (will inject on next prompt)
  │   │       └─ NO → spawnDetachedWingmanApply() [detached subprocess]
  │   └─ outputWingmanStopNotification() [systemMessage only, no context injection]
  │
  └─ (Stop hook returns, Stop JSON message sent to stdout)

[Detached subprocess runs in background]
  entire wingman __apply <repo-root>
    └─ runWingmanApply()
        └─ triggerAutoApply()
            └─ claude --continue --permission-mode acceptEdits <instruction>
                (This creates a NEW session, NOT injected into current one)
```

### 8. **Key Finding: No Auto-Loop Possible via Stop Hook**

**Why**:
1. Stop hook can only output `systemMessage` (notifications), not `additionalContext`
2. Stop hook fires AFTER session transitions to IDLE
3. Stop hook cannot return a "next prompt" - it just sends JSON to stdout
4. Auto-apply is handled by detached subprocess, not hook injection
5. To trigger an auto-loop, you'd need to modify `UserPromptSubmit` hook (line 78-84 of wingman_lifecycle.go), which DOES support context injection

**Current wingman approach**:
- **When live session exists**: Next UserPromptSubmit hook injects `wingmanApplyInstruction` as additionalContext (lines 78-84)
- **When NO live session**: Detached subprocess spawns `claude --continue` (background)

Neither path creates a hook-based auto-loop through the Stop hook.

## Summary: Ralph/Loop-Agent Re-Prompting and Claude Code Hook Protocol

Based on my systematic search of the codebase, here are my key findings:

### 1. **No Ralph/Loop-Agent References Found**

- This indicates that any loop-agent pattern would be a new plugin design, not built into the current CLI

### 2. **Stop Hook Protocol: NO Re-Prompting Support**

The Claude Code hook protocol **does NOT support re-prompting from Stop hooks**. Here's what I found:

**Hook Response Format (from `/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/hooks.go` lines 41-44):**
```go
type HookResponse struct {
    Continue   bool   `json:"continue"`
    StopReason string `json:"stopReason,omitempty"`
}
```

**Key Finding:** The `Continue` and `StopReason` fields are **only used by UserPromptSubmit hooks**, NOT Stop hooks:

**From `/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/docs/architecture/claude-hooks-integration.md` line 20-23:**
```
Prompt blocking - UserPromptSubmit hook needs to support returning a response to be shown in the cli session.
- Claude Code allows us to return a JSON response to stdout that can:
  - Allow continuation: {"continue": true}
  - Block with message: {"continue": false, "stopReason": "Your message here"}
```

### 3. **How additionalContext Actually Works**

The **only** re-prompting mechanism in the codebase is via `additionalContext` on **UserPromptSubmit hooks**:

**From `/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/cmd/entire/cli/hooks.go` lines 235-265:**
```go
type hookSpecificOutput struct {
    HookEventName     string `json:"hookEventName"`
    AdditionalContext string `json:"additionalContext,omitempty"`
}

type hookResponse struct {
    SystemMessage      string              `json:"systemMessage,omitempty"`
    HookSpecificOutput *hookSpecificOutput `json:"hookSpecificOutput,omitempty"`
}

func outputHookResponse(additionalContext string) error {
    resp := hookResponse{
        SystemMessage: additionalContext,
        HookSpecificOutput: &hookSpecificOutput{
            HookEventName:     "SessionStart",
            AdditionalContext: additionalContext,
        },
    }
    // ...
}
```

### 4. **Stop Hook Behavior**

The **Stop hook does NOT support hook response fields**. From `/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/lifecycle.go` lines 161-172:

```go
func (c *ClaudeCodeAgent) parseTurnEnd(stdin io.Reader) (*agent.Event, error) {
    raw, err := agent.ReadAndParseHookInput[sessionInfoRaw](stdin)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    return &agent.Event{
        Type:       agent.TurnEnd,
        SessionID:  raw.SessionID,
        SessionRef: raw.TranscriptPath,
        Timestamp:  time.Now(),
    }, nil
}
```

The Stop hook only extracts `SessionID` and transcript path - it returns immediately after processing with no response mechanism.

### 5. **How the CLI Actually Achieves Loop-Like Behavior**

The CLI **cannot make a Stop hook cause re-prompting directly**. However, Wingman provides an **alternative pattern** that achieves looping:

**From `/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/wingman_lifecycle.go` lines 47-101 and `/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/docs/architecture/wingman.md` lines 73-85:**

```
User sends prompt → UserPromptSubmit hook fires
                  → REVIEW.md exists on disk
                  → Inject as additionalContext (mandatory agent instruction)
                  → Agent reads REVIEW.md, applies suggestions, deletes file
                  → Agent then proceeds with user's actual request
```

This creates an effective loop:
1. Stop hook triggers wingman review (writes to REVIEW.md)
2. Next UserPromptSubmit hook injects REVIEW.md via `additionalContext`
3. Agent is forced to address the review before user's request
4. Process repeats if needed

### 6. **Key Files for Hook Implementation**

**Files that handle Stop hooks (NO re-prompting capability):**
- `/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go` (lines 160-172) - Stop hook parsing
- `/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/cmd/entire/cli/wingman_lifecycle.go` (lines 103-132) - Stop hook actions

**Files that handle UserPromptSubmit hooks (WITH re-prompting via additionalContext):**
- `/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go` (lines 113-158) - UserPromptSubmit processing
- `/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/cmd/entire/cli/hooks.go` (lines 235-294) - Hook response formatting
- `/Users/dip/Repositories/cli/cmd/entire/cli/wingman_lifecycle.go` (lines 47-101) - Wingman context injection

### 7. **Conclusion**

A Ralph/loop-agent style plugin **cannot be implemented using Stop hooks** because:

1. **Stop hooks have no response mechanism** - they execute to completion with no way to influence Claude's behavior
2. **Only UserPromptSubmit supports `continue: false` blocking** - this stops the prompt but doesn't re-prompt automatically
3. **Only UserPromptSubmit supports `additionalContext`** - this is injected when the user submits their NEXT prompt

**The right approach for a loop agent would be:**
- Use UserPromptSubmit hook to check for "loop" conditions
- If detected, return `additionalContext` with re-prompting instructions
- This forces the agent to re-evaluate before proceeding with the user's actual request
- Can repeat across multiple UserPromptSubmit invocations

This is essentially what Wingman does - it achieves looping through UserPromptSubmit injection, not Stop hook responses.

   103→// handleWingmanTurnEnd handles wingman actions at turn end: triggering reviews,
   104→// auto-applying pending reviews, and showing stop notifications.
   105→func handleWingmanTurnEnd(sessionID string, totalChanges int, relModifiedFiles, relNewFiles, relDeletedFiles, allPrompts []string, commitMessage string) {
   106→	repoRoot, err := paths.RepoRoot()
   107→	if err != nil {
   108→		return
   109→	}
   110→
   111→	strat := GetStrategy()
   112→
   113→	// Trigger wingman review for auto-commit strategy (commit already happened
   114→	// in SaveStep). Manual-commit triggers wingman from the git post-commit hook
   115→	// instead, since the user commits manually.
   116→	if totalChanges > 0 && strat.Name() == strategy.StrategyNameAutoCommit && settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {
   117→		triggerWingmanReview(WingmanPayload{
   118→			SessionID:     sessionID,
   119→			RepoRoot:      repoRoot,
   120→			ModifiedFiles: relModifiedFiles,
   121→			NewFiles:      relNewFiles,
   122→			DeletedFiles:  relDeletedFiles,
   123→			Prompts:       allPrompts,
   124→			CommitMessage: commitMessage,
   125→		})
   126→	}
   127→
   128→	// Auto-apply pending wingman review on turn end
   129→	triggerWingmanAutoApplyIfPending(repoRoot)
   130→
   131→	outputWingmanStopNotification(repoRoot)
   132→}
   133→
   134→// triggerWingmanAutoApplyIfPending checks for a pending REVIEW.md and spawns
   135→// the auto-apply subprocess if conditions are met. Called from the stop hook
   136→// on every turn end (both with-changes and no-changes paths).
   137→//
   138→// When a live session exists, this is a no-op: the prompt-submit injection
   139→// will deliver the review visibly in the user's terminal instead. Background
   140→// auto-apply is only used when no sessions are alive (all ended).
   141→func triggerWingmanAutoApplyIfPending(repoRoot string) {
   142→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "wingman")
   143→	if !settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {
   144→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply skip: wingman not enabled")
   145→		return
   146→	}
   147→	if os.Getenv("ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY") != "" {
   148→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply skip: already in apply subprocess")
   149→		return
   150→	}
   151→	reviewPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)
   152→	if _, statErr := os.Stat(reviewPath); statErr != nil {
   153→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply skip: no REVIEW.md pending")
   154→		return
   155→	}
   156→	// Skip auto-apply if the review has no actionable issues
   157→	if !reviewHasActionableIssues(reviewPath) {
   158→		logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply skip: review has no actionable issues, cleaning up")
   159→		_ = os.Remove(reviewPath)
   160→		return
   161→	}
   162→	wingmanState := loadWingmanStateDirect(repoRoot)
   163→	if wingmanState != nil && wingmanState.ApplyAttemptedAt != nil {
   164→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply already attempted, skipping",
   165→			slog.Time("attempted_at", *wingmanState.ApplyAttemptedAt),
   166→		)
   167→		return
   168→	}
   169→	// Don't spawn background auto-apply if a live session exists.
   170→	// The prompt-submit hook will inject REVIEW.md as additionalContext,
   171→	// which is visible to the user in their terminal.
   172→	if hasAnyLiveSession(repoRoot) {
   173→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply deferred: live session will handle via injection")
   174→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Review pending — will be injected on next prompt\n")
   175→		return
   176→	}
   177→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Pending review found, spawning auto-apply (no live sessions)\n")
   178→	logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman auto-apply spawning (no live sessions)",
   179→		slog.String("review_path", reviewPath),
   180→	)
   181→	spawnDetachedWingmanApply(repoRoot)
   182→}
   183→
   184→// reviewHasActionableIssues reads a REVIEW.md and checks if it contains
   185→// actionable issue markers ([CRITICAL], [WARNING], or [SUGGESTION]).
   186→// Returns false if the file can't be read or contains no issues.
   187→func reviewHasActionableIssues(reviewPath string) bool {
   188→	data, err := os.ReadFile(reviewPath) //nolint:gosec // path is from repo-relative constant
   189→	if err != nil {
   190→		return false
   191→	}
   192→
   193→	content := string(data)
   194→
   195→	// The review format uses "### [SEVERITY] description" for each issue.
   196→	// Check for any of the severity markers in heading context.
   197→	for _, marker := range []string{"[CRITICAL]", "[WARNING]", "[SUGGESTION]"} {
   198→		if strings.Contains(content, marker) {
   199→			return true
   200→		}
   201→	}
   202→
   203→	return false
   204→}
   205→
   206→// outputWingmanStopNotification outputs a systemMessage notification about
   207→// wingman status at the end of a stop hook. This makes wingman activity visible
   208→// in the agent terminal without injecting context into the agent's conversation.
   209→// Best-effort: status may be stale due to concurrent wingman processes.
   210→func outputWingmanStopNotification(repoRoot string) {
   211→	if !settings.IsWingmanEnabled() {
   212→		return
   213→	}
   214→	if os.Getenv("ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY") != "" {
   215→		return
   216→	}
   217→
   218→	lockPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanLockFile)
   219→	if info, err := os.Stat(lockPath); err == nil && time.Since(info.ModTime()) <= wingmanNotificationLockThreshold {
   220→		_ = outputHookMessage("[Wingman] Reviewing your changes...") //nolint:errcheck // best-effort notification
   221→		return
   222→	}
   223→
   224→	reviewPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)
   225→	if _, err := os.Stat(reviewPath); err == nil && reviewHasActionableIssues(reviewPath) {
   226→		_ = outputHookMessage("[Wingman] Review pending \u2014 will be addressed on your next prompt") //nolint:errcheck // best-effort notification
   227→		return
   228→	}
   229→}

   220→	if input.AgentID != "" {

   235→// hookSpecificOutput contains event-specific fields nested under hookSpecificOutput
   236→// in the hook response JSON. Claude Code requires this nesting for additionalContext
   237→// to be injected into the agent's conversation.
   238→type hookSpecificOutput struct {
   239→	HookEventName     string `json:"hookEventName"`
   240→	AdditionalContext string `json:"additionalContext,omitempty"`
   241→}
   242→
   243→// hookResponse represents a JSON response to a hook.
   244→// systemMessage is shown to the user as a warning/info message.
   245→// hookSpecificOutput contains event-specific fields like additionalContext.
   246→type hookResponse struct {
   247→	SystemMessage      string              `json:"systemMessage,omitempty"`
   248→	HookSpecificOutput *hookSpecificOutput `json:"hookSpecificOutput,omitempty"`
   249→}
   250→
   251→// outputHookResponse outputs a JSON response with additionalContext for
   252→// SessionStart hooks. The context is injected into the agent's conversation.
   253→func outputHookResponse(additionalContext string) error {
   254→	resp := hookResponse{
   255→		SystemMessage: additionalContext,
   256→		HookSpecificOutput: &hookSpecificOutput{
   257→			HookEventName:     "SessionStart",
   258→			AdditionalContext: additionalContext,
   259→		},
   260→	}
   261→	if err := json.NewEncoder(os.Stdout).Encode(resp); err != nil {
   262→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to encode hook response: %w", err)
   263→	}
   264→	return nil
   265→}
   266→
   267→// outputHookMessage outputs a JSON response with only a systemMessage — shown
   268→// to the user in the terminal but NOT injected into the agent's conversation.
   269→// Use this for informational notifications (e.g., wingman status) that the user
   270→// should see but the agent should not act on.
   271→func outputHookMessage(message string) error {
   272→	resp := hookResponse{SystemMessage: message}
   273→	if err := json.NewEncoder(os.Stdout).Encode(resp); err != nil {
   274→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to encode hook response: %w", err)
   275→	}
   276→	return nil
   277→}
   278→
   279→// outputHookResponseWithContextAndMessage outputs a JSON response with both
   280→// additionalContext (injected into agent conversation) and a systemMessage

   282→func outputHookResponseWithContextAndMessage(additionalContext, message string) error {
   283→	resp := hookResponse{

   285→		HookSpecificOutput: &hookSpecificOutput{
   286→			HookEventName:     "UserPromptSubmit",
   287→			AdditionalContext: additionalContext,
   288→		},
   289→	}
   290→	if err := json.NewEncoder(os.Stdout).Encode(resp); err != nil {
   291→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to encode hook response: %w", err)
   292→	}
   293→	return nil
   294→}

     1→// lifecycle.go implements the generic lifecycle event dispatcher.
     2→// It routes normalized events from any agent to the appropriate framework actions.
     3→//
     4→// The dispatcher inverts the current flow from "agent handler calls framework functions"
     5→// to "framework dispatcher calls agent methods." Agents are passive data providers;
     6→// the dispatcher handles all orchestration: state transitions, strategy calls,
     7→// file change detection, metadata generation.

     9→

    11→	"context"

    29→// DispatchLifecycleEvent routes a normalized lifecycle event to the appropriate handler.
    30→// Returns nil if the event was handled successfully.
    31→func DispatchLifecycleEvent(ag agent.Agent, event *agent.Event) error {
    32→	if ag == nil {
    33→		return errors.New("agent cannot be nil")
    34→	}
    35→	if event == nil {
    36→		return errors.New("event cannot be nil")
    37→	}
    38→
    39→	switch event.Type {
    40→	case agent.SessionStart:
    41→		return handleLifecycleSessionStart(ag, event)
    42→	case agent.TurnStart:
    43→		return handleLifecycleTurnStart(ag, event)
    44→	case agent.TurnEnd:
    45→		return handleLifecycleTurnEnd(ag, event)
    46→	case agent.Compaction:
    47→		return handleLifecycleCompaction(ag, event)
    48→	case agent.SessionEnd:
    49→		return handleLifecycleSessionEnd(ag, event)
    50→	case agent.SubagentStart:
    51→		return handleLifecycleSubagentStart(ag, event)
    52→	case agent.SubagentEnd:
    53→		return handleLifecycleSubagentEnd(ag, event)
    54→	default:
    55→		return fmt.Errorf("unknown lifecycle event type: %d", event.Type)
    56→	}
    57→}
    58→
    59→// handleLifecycleSessionStart handles session start: shows banner, checks concurrent sessions,
    60→// fires state machine transition.
    61→func handleLifecycleSessionStart(ag agent.Agent, event *agent.Event) error {
    62→	logCtx := logging.WithAgent(logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "lifecycle"), ag.Name())
    63→	logging.Info(logCtx, "session-start",
    64→		slog.String("event", event.Type.String()),
    65→		slog.String("session_id", event.SessionID),
    66→		slog.String("session_ref", event.SessionRef),
    67→	)
    68→
    69→	if event.SessionID == "" {
    70→		return fmt.Errorf("no session_id in %s event", event.Type)
    71→	}
    72→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(event.SessionID); err != nil {
    73→		return fmt.Errorf("invalid %s event: %w", event.Type, err)
    74→	}
    75→
    76→	// Build informational message
    77→	message := "\n\nPowered by Entire:\n  This conversation will be linked to your next commit."
    78→
    79→	// Append wingman status if enabled
    80→	message = appendWingmanSessionStartStatus(message)
    81→
    82→	// Check for concurrent sessions and append count if any
    83→	strat := GetStrategy()
    84→	if concurrentChecker, ok := strat.(strategy.ConcurrentSessionChecker); ok {
    85→		if count, err := concurrentChecker.CountOtherActiveSessionsWithCheckpoints(event.SessionID); err == nil && count > 0 {
    86→			message += fmt.Sprintf("\n  %d other active conversation(s) in this workspace will also be included.\n  Use 'entire status' for more information.", count)
    87→		}
    88→	}
    89→
    90→	// Output informational message
    91→	if event.ResponseMessage != "" {
    92→		message = event.ResponseMessage
    93→	}
    94→	if err := outputHookResponse(message); err != nil {
    95→		return err
    96→	}
    97→
    98→	// Fire EventSessionStart for the current session (if state exists).
    99→	if state, loadErr := strategy.LoadSessionState(event.SessionID); loadErr != nil {
   100→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to load session state on start: %v\n", loadErr)
   101→	} else if state != nil {
   102→		if transErr := strategy.TransitionAndLog(state, session.EventSessionStart, session.TransitionContext{}, session.NoOpActionHandler{}); transErr != nil {
   103→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: session start transition failed: %v\n", transErr)
   104→		}
   105→		if saveErr := strategy.SaveSessionState(state); saveErr != nil {
   106→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to update session state on start: %v\n", saveErr)
   107→		}
   108→	}
   109→
   110→	return nil
   111→}

   113→// handleLifecycleTurnStart handles turn start: captures pre-prompt state,
   114→// ensures strategy setup, initializes session.
   115→func handleLifecycleTurnStart(ag agent.Agent, event *agent.Event) error {
   116→	logCtx := logging.WithAgent(logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "lifecycle"), ag.Name())
   117→	logging.Info(logCtx, "turn-start",
   118→		slog.String("event", event.Type.String()),

   120→		slog.String("session_ref", event.SessionRef),
   121→	)
   122→
   123→	sessionID := event.SessionID
   124→	if sessionID == "" {
   125→		return fmt.Errorf("no session_id in %s event", event.Type)
   126→	}
   127→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(sessionID); err != nil {
   128→		return fmt.Errorf("invalid %s event: %w", event.Type, err)
   129→	}
   130→
   131→	// Capture pre-prompt state (including transcript position via TranscriptAnalyzer)
   132→	if err := CapturePrePromptState(ag, sessionID, event.SessionRef); err != nil {
   133→		return err
   134→	}
   135→
   136→	// If a wingman review is pending, inject it as additionalContext so the
   137→	// agent addresses it BEFORE the user's request. Must return early to
   138→	// avoid corrupting the JSON stdout with additional output.
   139→	if handleWingmanTurnStart(sessionID) {
   140→		return nil
   141→	}
   142→
   143→	// Ensure strategy setup and initialize session
   144→	strat := GetStrategy()
   145→
   146→	if err := strat.EnsureSetup(); err != nil {

   148→	}
   149→
   150→	if initializer, ok := strat.(strategy.SessionInitializer); ok {
   151→		agentType := ag.Type()
   152→		if err := initializer.InitializeSession(sessionID, agentType, event.SessionRef, event.Prompt); err != nil {
   153→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to initialize session state: %v\n", err)
   154→		}
   155→	}

   157→	return nil
   158→}

   160→// handleLifecycleTurnEnd handles turn end: validates transcript, extracts metadata,

   164→func handleLifecycleTurnEnd(ag agent.Agent, event *agent.Event) error {

   431→// handleLifecycleCompaction handles context compaction: saves current progress
   432→// but stays in ACTIVE phase (unlike TurnEnd which transitions to IDLE).
   433→// Also resets the transcript offset since the transcript may be truncated.
   434→func handleLifecycleCompaction(ag agent.Agent, event *agent.Event) error {
   435→	logCtx := logging.WithAgent(logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "lifecycle"), ag.Name())
   436→	logging.Info(logCtx, "compaction",
   437→		slog.String("event", event.Type.String()),
   438→		slog.String("session_id", event.SessionID),
   439→	)
   440→
   441→	// Fire EventCompaction to trigger ActionCondenseIfFilesTouched (stays in ACTIVE)
   442→	sessionID := event.SessionID
   443→	sessionState, loadErr := strategy.LoadSessionState(sessionID)
   444→	if loadErr != nil {
   445→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to load session state for compaction: %v\n", loadErr)
   446→	}
   447→	if sessionState != nil {
   448→		if transErr := strategy.TransitionAndLog(sessionState, session.EventCompaction, session.TransitionContext{}, session.NoOpActionHandler{}); transErr != nil {
   449→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: compaction transition failed: %v\n", transErr)
   450→		}
   451→
   452→		// Reset transcript offset since the transcript may be truncated/reorganized
   453→		sessionState.CheckpointTranscriptStart = 0
   454→
   455→		if saveErr := strategy.SaveSessionState(sessionState); saveErr != nil {
   456→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to save session state after compaction: %v\n", saveErr)
   457→		}
   458→	}
   459→
   460→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Context compaction: transcript offset reset\n")
   461→	return nil
   462→}
   463→
   464→// handleLifecycleSessionEnd handles session end: marks the session as ended.
   465→func handleLifecycleSessionEnd(ag agent.Agent, event *agent.Event) error {
   466→	logCtx := logging.WithAgent(logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "lifecycle"), ag.Name())
   467→	logging.Info(logCtx, "session-end",
   468→		slog.String("event", event.Type.String()),
   469→		slog.String("session_id", event.SessionID),
   470→	)
   471→
   472→	if event.SessionID == "" {
   473→		return nil // No session to update
   474→	}
   475→
   476→	if err := markSessionEnded(event.SessionID); err != nil {
   477→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to mark session ended: %v\n", err)
   478→	}
   479→	return nil
   480→}

   505→// handleLifecycleSubagentEnd handles subagent end: detects changes, saves task checkpoint.
   506→func handleLifecycleSubagentEnd(ag agent.Agent, event *agent.Event) error {
   507→	logCtx := logging.WithAgent(logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "lifecycle"), ag.Name())

   514→
   515→	// Extract subagent type and description from tool input

   517→
   518→	// Determine subagent transcript path
   519→	transcriptDir := filepath.Dir(event.SessionRef)
   520→	var subagentTranscriptPath string
   521→	if event.SubagentID != "" {

   523→		if !fileExists(subagentTranscriptPath) {

   528→	// Log context

   532→	if event.SubagentID != "" {

   534→	}

   539→	// Extract modified files from subagent transcript
   540→	var modifiedFiles []string
   541→	if analyzer, ok := ag.(agent.TranscriptAnalyzer); ok {
   542→		transcriptToScan := event.SessionRef
   543→		if subagentTranscriptPath != "" {
   544→			transcriptToScan = subagentTranscriptPath

   546→		if files, _, fileErr := analyzer.ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset(transcriptToScan, 0); fileErr != nil {
   547→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to extract modified files from subagent: %v\n", fileErr)
   548→		} else {
   549→			modifiedFiles = files

   551→	}

   553→	// Load pre-task state and detect file changes

   563→	if err != nil {

   565→	}

   569→	if err != nil {

   571→	}

   574→	var relNewFiles, relDeletedFiles []string
   575→	if changes != nil {
   576→		relNewFiles = FilterAndNormalizePaths(changes.New, repoRoot)
   577→		relDeletedFiles = FilterAndNormalizePaths(changes.Deleted, repoRoot)
   578→	}
   579→

   587→	// Find checkpoint UUID from main transcript (best-effort)

   601→	// Build task checkpoint context
   602→	strat := GetStrategy()
   603→	agentType := ag.Type()
   604→
   605→	ctx := strategy.TaskStepContext{

   622→	if err := strat.SaveTaskStep(ctx); err != nil {

   624→	}

   626→	_ = CleanupPreTaskState(event.ToolUseID) //nolint:errcheck // best-effort cleanup
   627→	return nil
   628→}

   630→// --- Helper functions ---
   631→
   632→// resolveTranscriptOffset determines the transcript offset to use for parsing.
   633→// Prefers pre-prompt state, falls back to session state.
   634→func resolveTranscriptOffset(preState *PrePromptState, sessionID string) int {
   635→	if preState != nil && preState.TranscriptOffset > 0 {
   636→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Pre-prompt state found: parsing transcript from offset %d\n", preState.TranscriptOffset)
   637→		return preState.TranscriptOffset
   638→	}
   639→
   640→	// Fall back to session state (e.g., auto-commit strategy updates it after each save)
   641→	sessionState, loadErr := strategy.LoadSessionState(sessionID)
   642→	if loadErr != nil {
   643→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to load session state: %v\n", loadErr)
   644→		return 0
   645→	}
   646→	if sessionState != nil && sessionState.CheckpointTranscriptStart > 0 {
   647→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Session state found: parsing transcript from offset %d\n", sessionState.CheckpointTranscriptStart)
   648→		return sessionState.CheckpointTranscriptStart
   649→	}
   650→
   651→	return 0
   652→}
   653→
   654→// updateAutoCommitTranscriptPosition updates the session state with the new transcript position
   655→// for the auto-commit strategy.
   656→func updateAutoCommitTranscriptPosition(sessionID string, newPosition int) {
   657→	sessionState, loadErr := strategy.LoadSessionState(sessionID)
   658→	if loadErr != nil {
   659→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to load session state: %v\n", loadErr)
   660→		return
   661→	}
   662→	if sessionState == nil {
   663→		sessionState = &strategy.SessionState{
   664→			SessionID: sessionID,
   665→		}
   666→	}
   667→	sessionState.CheckpointTranscriptStart = newPosition
   668→	sessionState.StepCount++
   669→	if updateErr := strategy.SaveSessionState(sessionState); updateErr != nil {
   670→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to update session state: %v\n", updateErr)
   671→	} else {
   672→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Updated session state: transcript position=%d, checkpoint=%d\n",
   673→			newPosition, sessionState.StepCount)
   674→	}
   675→}
   676→
   677→// createContextFile creates a context.md file for the session checkpoint.
   678→// This is a unified version that works for all agents.
   679→func createContextFile(contextFile, commitMessage, sessionID string, prompts []string, summary string) error {
   680→	var sb strings.Builder
   681→
   682→	sb.WriteString("# Session Context\n\n")
   683→	fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "Session ID: %s\n", sessionID)
   684→	fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "Commit Message: %s\n\n", commitMessage)
   685→
   686→	if len(prompts) > 0 {
   687→		sb.WriteString("## Prompts\n\n")
   688→		for i, p := range prompts {
   689→			fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "### Prompt %d\n\n%s\n\n", i+1, p)
   690→		}
   691→	}
   692→
   693→	if summary != "" {
   694→		sb.WriteString("## Summary\n\n")
   695→		sb.WriteString(summary)
   696→		sb.WriteString("\n")
   697→	}
   698→
   699→	if err := os.WriteFile(contextFile, []byte(sb.String()), 0o600); err != nil {
   700→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to write context file: %w", err)
   701→	}
   702→	return nil
   703→}
   704→
   705→// parseTranscriptForCheckpointUUID is a thin wrapper around transcript parsing for checkpoint UUID lookup.
   706→// Returns parsed transcript lines for use with FindCheckpointUUID.
   707→func parseTranscriptForCheckpointUUID(transcriptPath string) ([]transcriptLine, int, error) {
   708→	lines, total, err := transcript.ParseFromFileAtLine(transcriptPath, 0)
   709→	if err != nil {
   710→		return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("parsing transcript for checkpoint UUID: %w", err)
   711→	}
   712→	return lines, total, nil
   713→}

   715→// transitionSessionTurnEnd transitions the session phase to IDLE and dispatches turn-end actions.
   716→func transitionSessionTurnEnd(sessionID string) {
   717→	turnState, loadErr := strategy.LoadSessionState(sessionID)
   718→	if loadErr != nil {
   719→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to load session state for turn end: %v\n", loadErr)
   720→		return
   721→	}
   722→	if turnState == nil {
   723→		return
   724→	}
   725→	if err := strategy.TransitionAndLog(turnState, session.EventTurnEnd, session.TransitionContext{}, session.NoOpActionHandler{}); err != nil {
   726→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: turn-end transition failed: %v\n", err)
   727→	}
   728→
   729→	// Always dispatch to strategy for turn-end handling. The strategy reads
   730→	// work items from state (e.g. TurnCheckpointIDs), not the action list.
   731→	strat := GetStrategy()
   732→	if handler, ok := strat.(strategy.TurnEndHandler); ok {
   733→		if err := handler.HandleTurnEnd(turnState); err != nil {
   734→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: turn-end action dispatch failed: %v\n", err)
   735→		}
   736→	}
   737→
   738→	if updateErr := strategy.SaveSessionState(turnState); updateErr != nil {
   739→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: failed to update session phase on turn end: %v\n", updateErr)
   740→	}
   741→}
   742→
   743→// markSessionEnded transitions the session to ENDED phase via the state machine.
   744→func markSessionEnded(sessionID string) error {
   745→	state, err := strategy.LoadSessionState(sessionID)
   746→	if err != nil {
   747→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to load session state: %w", err)
   748→	}
   749→	if state == nil {
   750→		return nil // No state file, nothing to update
   751→	}
   752→
   753→	if transErr := strategy.TransitionAndLog(state, session.EventSessionStop, session.TransitionContext{}, session.NoOpActionHandler{}); transErr != nil {
   754→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Warning: session stop transition failed: %v\n", transErr)
   755→	}
   756→
   757→	now := time.Now()
   758→	state.EndedAt = &now
   759→
   760→	if err := strategy.SaveSessionState(state); err != nil {
   761→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to save session state: %w", err)
   762→	}
   763→	return nil
   764→}

   766→// logFileChanges logs the files modified, created, and deleted during a session.

    58→func runWingmanReview(payloadPath string) error {

    62→	// Read payload from file (avoids OS argv limits with large payloads)

    74→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to unmarshal payload: %w", err)

    80→		return errors.New("repo_root is required in payload")

    87→	// Clean up lock file when review completes (regardless of success/failure)
    88→	lockPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanLockFile)

    91→			wingmanLog("WARNING: failed to remove lock file: %v", err)

    95→	}()
    96→
    97→	// Initial delay: let the agent turn fully settle

    99→	time.Sleep(wingmanInitialDelay)

   148→	wingmanLog("review received: %d bytes in %s", len(reviewText), time.Since(reviewStart).Round(time.Millisecond))

   150→	// Write REVIEW.md
   151→	reviewPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)
   152→	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(reviewPath), 0o750); err != nil {
   153→		wingmanLog("ERROR creating directory: %v", err)
   154→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create directory: %w", err)
   155→	}
   156→	//nolint:gosec // G306: review file is not secrets
   157→	if err := os.WriteFile(reviewPath, []byte(reviewText), 0o644); err != nil {
   158→		wingmanLog("ERROR writing REVIEW.md: %v", err)
   159→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to write REVIEW.md: %w", err)
   160→	}
   161→	wingmanLog("REVIEW.md written to %s", reviewPath)
   162→
   163→	// Update dedup state — write directly to known path instead of using
   164→	// os.Chdir (which mutates process-wide state).
   165→	allFilePaths := make([]string, 0, len(payload.ModifiedFiles)+len(payload.NewFiles)+len(payload.DeletedFiles))
   166→	allFilePaths = append(allFilePaths, payload.ModifiedFiles...)
   167→	allFilePaths = append(allFilePaths, payload.NewFiles...)
   168→	allFilePaths = append(allFilePaths, payload.DeletedFiles...)
   169→
   170→	saveWingmanStateDirect(repoRoot, &WingmanState{
   171→		SessionID:     payload.SessionID,
   172→		FilesHash:     computeFilesHash(allFilePaths),
   173→		ReviewedAt:    time.Now(),
   174→		ReviewApplied: false,
   175→	})
   176→	wingmanLog("dedup state saved")
   177→
   178→	// If any session is live (IDLE/ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED), don't auto-apply
   179→	// in the background. The prompt-submit hook will inject REVIEW.md as
   180→	// additionalContext when the user sends their next prompt — this is VISIBLE
   181→	// in their terminal. Only use background auto-apply when no sessions are
   182→	// alive (e.g., user closed all sessions).
   183→	if hasAnyLiveSession(repoRoot) {
   184→		wingmanLog("live session detected, deferring to prompt-submit injection (visible)")
   185→		return nil
   186→	}
   187→
   188→	// No live sessions — apply in background as fallback
   189→	wingmanLog("no live sessions, triggering background auto-apply")
   190→	now := time.Now()
   191→	state := loadWingmanStateDirect(repoRoot)
   192→	if state != nil {
   193→		state.ApplyAttemptedAt = &now
   194→		saveWingmanStateDirect(repoRoot, state)
   195→	}
   196→
   197→	applyStart := time.Now()
   198→	if err := triggerAutoApply(repoRoot); err != nil {
   199→		wingmanLog("ERROR auto-apply failed after %s: %v", time.Since(applyStart).Round(time.Millisecond), err)
   200→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to trigger auto-apply: %w", err)
   201→	}
   202→	wingmanLog("auto-apply completed in %s", time.Since(applyStart).Round(time.Millisecond))
   203→
   204→	return nil
   205→}

   207→// computeDiff gets the full branch diff for review. It diffs the current HEAD
   208→// against the merge base with the default branch (main/master), giving the
   209→// reviewer a holistic view of all branch changes rather than just one commit.
   210→func computeDiff(repoRoot string) (string, error) {
   211→	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), wingmanGitTimeout)
   212→	defer cancel()
   213→
   214→	// Find the merge base with the default branch for a holistic branch diff.
   215→	mergeBase := findMergeBase(ctx, repoRoot)
   216→	if mergeBase != "" {
   217→		wingmanLog("using merge-base %s for branch diff", mergeBase)
   218→		diff, err := gitDiff(ctx, repoRoot, mergeBase)
   219→		if err == nil && strings.TrimSpace(diff) != "" {
   220→			return diff, nil
   221→		}
   222→		// Fall through to HEAD diff if merge-base diff fails or is empty
   223→	}
   224→
   225→	// Fallback: diff uncommitted changes against HEAD
   226→	wingmanLog("falling back to HEAD diff")
   227→	diff, err := gitDiff(ctx, repoRoot, "HEAD")
   228→	if err != nil {
   229→		return "", fmt.Errorf("git diff failed: %w", err)
   230→	}
   231→
   232→	// If no uncommitted changes, try the latest commit itself
   233→	if strings.TrimSpace(diff) == "" {
   234→		diff, err = gitDiff(ctx, repoRoot, "HEAD~1", "HEAD")
   235→		if err != nil {
   236→			return "", fmt.Errorf("git diff for latest commit failed: %w", err)
   237→		}
   238→	}
   239→
   240→	return diff, nil
   241→}
   242→
   243→// findMergeBase returns the merge-base commit between HEAD and the default
   244→// branch (tries main, then master). Returns empty string if not found.
   245→func findMergeBase(ctx context.Context, repoRoot string) string {
   246→	for _, branch := range []string{"main", "master"} {
   247→		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "merge-base", branch, "HEAD") //nolint:gosec // branch is from hardcoded slice
   248→		cmd.Dir = repoRoot
   249→		out, err := cmd.Output()
   250→		if err == nil {
   251→			return strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
   252→		}
   253→	}
   254→	return ""
   255→}
   256→
   257→// gitDiff runs git diff with the given args and returns stdout.
   258→func gitDiff(ctx context.Context, repoRoot string, args ...string) (string, error) {
   259→	fullArgs := append([]string{"diff"}, args...)
   260→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", fullArgs...) //nolint:gosec // args are from internal logic
   261→	cmd.Dir = repoRoot
   262→	var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
   263→	cmd.Stdout = &stdout
   264→	cmd.Stderr = &stderr
   265→	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
   266→		return "", fmt.Errorf("git diff %v: %w (stderr: %s)", args, err, stderr.String())
   267→	}
   268→	return stdout.String(), nil
   269→}

   271→// resolveWingmanModel returns the model to use for wingman reviews,
   272→// reading from settings with a fallback to the default.
   273→func resolveWingmanModel() string {
   274→	s, err := settings.Load()
   275→	if err != nil {
   276→		return wingmanDefaultReviewModel
   277→	}
   278→	if m := s.WingmanModel(); m != "" {
   279→		return m
   280→	}
   281→	return wingmanDefaultReviewModel
   282→}
   283→
   284→// resolveWingmanAgent returns the agent name to use for wingman reviews,
   285→// reading from settings with a fallback to the default agent.
   286→func resolveWingmanAgent() agent.AgentName {
   287→	s, err := settings.Load()
   288→	if err != nil {
   289→		return agent.DefaultAgentName
   290→	}
   291→	if a := s.WingmanAgent(); a != "" {
   292→		return agent.AgentName(a)
   293→	}
   294→	return agent.DefaultAgentName
   295→}
   296→
   297→// callAgentForReview invokes the configured agent's Prompter to perform a review.
   298→// repoRoot is the repository root so the reviewer can access the full codebase.
   299→func callAgentForReview(repoRoot, prompt, model string) (string, error) {
   300→	agentName := resolveWingmanAgent()
   301→
   302→	ag, err := agent.Get(agentName)
   303→	if err != nil {
   304→		return "", fmt.Errorf("wingman agent %q not found: %w", agentName, err)
   305→	}
   306→
   307→	prompter, ok := ag.(agent.Prompter)
   308→	if !ok {
   309→		return "", fmt.Errorf("agent %q does not support prompting (does not implement agent.Prompter)", agentName)
   310→	}
   311→
   312→	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), wingmanReviewTimeout)
   313→	defer cancel()
   314→
   315→	// Grant read-only tool access so the reviewer can inspect source files
   316→	// beyond just the diff. Permission bypass is safe here since tools are
   317→	// restricted to read-only operations.
   318→	result, err := prompter.Prompt(ctx, prompt, agent.PromptOptions{
   319→		Model:          model,
   320→		WorkDir:        repoRoot,
   321→		AllowedTools:   "Read,Glob,Grep",
   322→		PermissionMode: "bypassPermissions",
   323→	})
   324→	if err != nil {
   325→		return "", fmt.Errorf("agent review prompt failed: %w", err)
   326→	}
   327→
   328→	return result.Text, nil
   329→}
   330→
   331→// readSessionContext reads the context.md file from the session's checkpoint
   332→// metadata directory. Returns empty string if unavailable.
   333→func readSessionContext(repoRoot, sessionID string) string {
   334→	if sessionID == "" {
   335→		return ""
   336→	}
   337→	contextPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, ".entire", "metadata", sessionID, "context.md")
   338→	data, err := os.ReadFile(contextPath) //nolint:gosec // path constructed from repoRoot + session ID
   339→	if err != nil {
   340→		if !errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
   341→			wingmanLog("WARNING: failed to read session context: %v", err)
   342→		}
   343→		return ""
   344→	}
   345→	return string(data)
   346→}
   347→
   348→// staleActiveSessionThreshold is the maximum age of a session state file in an
   349→// ACTIVE phase before it is considered stale (crashed agent) and ignored by
   350→// hasAnyLiveSession. Only applies to ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED phases — an IDLE
   351→// session is always considered live regardless of age (user may just be away).
   352→const staleActiveSessionThreshold = 4 * time.Hour
   353→
   354→// hasAnyLiveSession checks if any session is in a non-ENDED phase (IDLE,
   355→// ACTIVE, or ACTIVE_COMMITTED). Used to decide whether to defer review
   356→// application to the prompt-submit injection (visible to user) vs background
   357→// auto-apply (invisible).
   358→//
   359→// ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED sessions older than staleActiveSessionThreshold are
   360→// skipped as likely orphaned from crashed processes. IDLE sessions are always
   361→// considered live regardless of age.
   362→func hasAnyLiveSession(repoRoot string) bool {
   363→	sessDir := findSessionStateDir(repoRoot)
   364→	if sessDir == "" {
   365→		return false
   366→	}
   367→
   368→	entries, err := os.ReadDir(sessDir)
   369→	if err != nil {
   370→		return false
   371→	}
   372→
   373→	const maxCheck = 50
   374→	checked := 0
   375→	for _, entry := range entries {
   376→		if checked >= maxCheck {
   377→			wingmanLog("stopping live-session scan after %d entries; assuming live session may exist", checked)
   378→			return true
   379→		}
   380→		name := entry.Name()
   381→		if !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".json") {
   382→			continue
   383→		}
   384→		checked++
   385→
   386→		sid := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".json")
   387→		info := readSessionPhaseInfo(sessDir, sid)
   388→		if info.Phase == "" || info.Phase == string(session.PhaseEnded) {
   389→			continue
   390→		}
   391→
   392→		// ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED sessions that haven't had a real agent
   393→		// interaction in a long time are likely orphaned from crashed agents.
   394→		// Uses LastInteractionTime from JSON (not file modtime) because
   395→		// PostCommit saves all session files on every commit, refreshing
   396→		// modtime even for stale sessions.
   397→		// IDLE sessions are always considered live (user may just be away).
   398→		if session.PhaseFromString(info.Phase).IsActive() {
   399→			if info.LastInteractionTime != nil && time.Since(*info.LastInteractionTime) > staleActiveSessionThreshold {
   400→				wingmanLog("skipping stale active session %s (phase=%s, last_interaction=%s ago)", sid, info.Phase, time.Since(*info.LastInteractionTime).Round(time.Second))
   401→				continue
   402→			}
   403→		}
   404→
   405→		wingmanLog("found live session %s (phase=%s)", sid, info.Phase)
   406→		return true
   407→	}
   408→
   409→	return false
   410→}
   411→
   412→// findSessionStateDir locates the .git/entire-sessions/ directory by
   413→// reading .git to handle both normal repos and worktrees.
   414→func findSessionStateDir(repoRoot string) string {
   415→	gitPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, ".git")
   416→	info, err := os.Stat(gitPath)
   417→	if err != nil {
   418→		return ""
   419→	}
   420→
   421→	var gitDir string
   422→	if info.IsDir() {
   423→		// Normal repo: .git is a directory
   424→		gitDir = gitPath
   425→	} else {
   426→		// Worktree: .git is a file containing "gitdir: <path>"
   427→		data, readErr := os.ReadFile(gitPath) //nolint:gosec // path from repoRoot
   428→		if readErr != nil {
   429→			return ""
   430→		}
   431→		content := strings.TrimSpace(string(data))
   432→		if !strings.HasPrefix(content, "gitdir: ") {
   433→			return ""
   434→		}
   435→		gitDir = strings.TrimPrefix(content, "gitdir: ")
   436→		if !filepath.IsAbs(gitDir) {
   437→			gitDir = filepath.Join(repoRoot, gitDir)
   438→		}
   439→		// For worktrees, session state is in the common dir
   440→		// .git/worktrees/<name> → ../../ is the common .git dir
   441→		commonDir := filepath.Join(gitDir, "..", "..")
   442→		gitDir = filepath.Clean(commonDir)
   443→	}
   444→
   445→	sessDir := filepath.Join(gitDir, "entire-sessions")
   446→	if _, statErr := os.Stat(sessDir); statErr != nil {
   447→		return ""
   448→	}
   449→	return sessDir
   450→}
   451→
   452→// sessionPhaseInfo holds the subset of session state needed for liveness checks.
   453→type sessionPhaseInfo struct {
   454→	Phase               string
   455→	LastInteractionTime *time.Time
   456→}
   457→
   458→func readSessionPhaseInfo(sessDir, sessionID string) sessionPhaseInfo {
   459→	data, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(sessDir, sessionID+".json")) //nolint:gosec // sessDir is from git internals
   460→	if err != nil {
   461→		return sessionPhaseInfo{}
   462→	}
   463→	var partial struct {
   464→		Phase               string     `json:"phase"`
   465→		LastInteractionTime *time.Time `json:"last_interaction_time,omitempty"`
   466→	}
   467→	if json.Unmarshal(data, &partial) != nil {
   468→		return sessionPhaseInfo{}
   469→	}
   470→	return sessionPhaseInfo{
   471→		Phase:               partial.Phase,
   472→		LastInteractionTime: partial.LastInteractionTime,
   473→	}
   474→}
   475→
   476→// runWingmanApply is the entrypoint for the __apply subcommand, spawned by the
   477→// stop hook when a pending REVIEW.md is detected. It re-checks preconditions
   478→// and triggers claude --continue to apply the review.
   479→func runWingmanApply(repoRoot string) error {
   480→	wingmanLog("apply process started (pid=%d)", os.Getpid())
   481→
   482→	reviewPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanReviewFile)
   483→	if !fileExists(reviewPath) {
   484→		wingmanLog("no REVIEW.md found at %s, nothing to apply", reviewPath)
   485→		return nil
   486→	}
   487→	wingmanLog("REVIEW.md found at %s", reviewPath)
   488→
   489→	// Retry prevention: check if apply was already attempted for this review
   490→	state := loadWingmanStateDirect(repoRoot)
   491→	switch {
   492→	case state == nil:
   493→		wingmanLog("no wingman state found, proceeding without session check")
   494→	case state.ApplyAttemptedAt != nil:
   495→		wingmanLog("apply already attempted at %s, skipping", state.ApplyAttemptedAt.Format(time.RFC3339))
   496→		return nil
   497→	default:
   498→		wingmanLog("wingman state loaded: session=%s", state.SessionID)
   499→	}
   500→
   501→	// Re-check session hasn't become active (user may have typed during spawn delay).
   502→	// IDLE and ENDED are safe — only ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED should block.
   503→	if state != nil && state.SessionID != "" {
   504→		sessDir := findSessionStateDir(repoRoot)
   505→		if sessDir != "" {
   506→			phaseInfo := readSessionPhaseInfo(sessDir, state.SessionID)
   507→			if phaseInfo.Phase != "" && session.PhaseFromString(phaseInfo.Phase).IsActive() {
   508→				wingmanLog("session is active (phase=%s), aborting (next stop hook will retry)", phaseInfo.Phase)
   509→				return nil
   510→			}
   511→			wingmanLog("session phase=%s, safe to proceed", phaseInfo.Phase)
   512→		}
   513→	}
   514→
   515→	// Mark apply as attempted BEFORE triggering
   516→	if state != nil {
   517→		now := time.Now()
   518→		state.ApplyAttemptedAt = &now
   519→		saveWingmanStateDirect(repoRoot, state)
   520→	}
   521→
   522→	wingmanLog("triggering auto-apply via claude --continue")
   523→	applyStart := time.Now()
   524→	if err := triggerAutoApply(repoRoot); err != nil {
   525→		wingmanLog("ERROR auto-apply failed after %s: %v", time.Since(applyStart).Round(time.Millisecond), err)
   526→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to trigger auto-apply: %w", err)
   527→	}
   528→	wingmanLog("auto-apply completed in %s", time.Since(applyStart).Round(time.Millisecond))
   529→
   530→	return nil
   531→}
   532→
   533→// triggerAutoApply spawns claude --continue to apply the review suggestions.
   534→// NOTE: This uses --continue which is Claude-specific and not part of the
   535→// Prompter interface. If the wingman agent is not claude-code, auto-apply
   536→// is skipped.
   537→func triggerAutoApply(repoRoot string) error {
   538→	agentName := resolveWingmanAgent()
   539→	if agentName != agent.AgentNameClaudeCode {
   540→		wingmanLog("auto-apply skipped: --continue is only supported for claude-code (agent=%s)", agentName)
   541→		return nil
   542→	}
   543→
   544→	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), wingmanApplyTimeout)
   545→	defer cancel()
   546→
   547→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "claude",
   548→		"--continue",
   549→		"--print",
   550→		"--setting-sources", "",
   551→		// Auto-accept edits so the agent can modify files and delete REVIEW.md
   552→		// without requiring user consent (this runs in a background process).
   553→		"--permission-mode", "acceptEdits",
   554→		wingmanApplyInstruction,
   555→	)
   556→	cmd.Dir = repoRoot
   557→	// Strip GIT_* env vars to prevent hook interference, and set
   558→	// ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY=1 so git hooks (post-commit) know not to
   559→	// trigger another wingman review (prevents infinite recursion).
   560→	env := agent.StripGitEnv(os.Environ())
   561→	env = append(env, "ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY=1")
   562→	cmd.Env = env
   563→
   564→	var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
   565→	cmd.Stdout = &stdout
   566→	cmd.Stderr = &stderr
   567→
   568→	return cmd.Run() //nolint:wrapcheck // caller wraps
   569→}
   570→
   571→// saveWingmanStateDirect writes the wingman state file directly to a known path
   572→// under repoRoot, avoiding os.Chdir (which mutates process-wide state).
   573→func saveWingmanStateDirect(repoRoot string, state *WingmanState) {
   574→	statePath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanStateFile)
   575→	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(statePath), 0o750); err != nil {
   576→		return
   577→	}
   578→	data, err := json.MarshalIndent(state, "", "  ")
   579→	if err != nil {
   580→		return
   581→	}
   582→	//nolint:gosec,errcheck // G306: state file is config, not secrets; best-effort write
   583→	_ = os.WriteFile(statePath, data, 0o644)
   584→}

   399→// triggerWingmanReview checks preconditions and spawns the detached review process.
   400→func triggerWingmanReview(payload WingmanPayload) {
   401→	// Prevent infinite recursion: if we're inside a wingman auto-apply,
   402→	// don't trigger another review. The env var is set by triggerAutoApply.
   403→	if os.Getenv("ENTIRE_WINGMAN_APPLY") != "" {
   404→		return
   405→	}
   406→
   407→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "wingman")
   408→	repoRoot := payload.RepoRoot
   409→
   410→	totalFiles := len(payload.ModifiedFiles) + len(payload.NewFiles) + len(payload.DeletedFiles)
   411→	logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman trigger evaluating",
   412→		slog.String("session_id", payload.SessionID),
   413→		slog.Int("file_count", totalFiles),
   414→	)
   415→
   416→	// Check if a pending REVIEW.md already exists for the current session
   417→	if shouldSkipPendingReview(repoRoot, payload.SessionID) {
   418→		logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman skipped: pending review exists for current session")
   419→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Pending review exists, skipping\n")
   420→		return
   421→	}
   422→
   423→	// Atomic lock file prevents concurrent review spawns. O_CREATE|O_EXCL
   424→	// is atomic on all platforms, avoiding the TOCTOU race of Stat+WriteFile.
   425→	lockPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, wingmanLockFile)
   426→	if !acquireWingmanLock(lockPath, payload.SessionID) {
   427→		logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman skipped: review already in progress")
   428→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Review in progress, skipping\n")
   429→		return
   430→	}
   431→
   432→	// Dedup check: compute hash of sorted file paths
   433→	allFiles := make([]string, 0, len(payload.ModifiedFiles)+len(payload.NewFiles)+len(payload.DeletedFiles))
   434→	allFiles = append(allFiles, payload.ModifiedFiles...)
   435→	allFiles = append(allFiles, payload.NewFiles...)
   436→	allFiles = append(allFiles, payload.DeletedFiles...)
   437→	filesHash := computeFilesHash(allFiles)
   438→
   439→	state, _ := loadWingmanState() //nolint:errcheck // best-effort dedup
   440→	if state != nil && state.FilesHash == filesHash && state.SessionID == payload.SessionID {
   441→		logging.Info(logCtx, "wingman skipped: dedup hash match",
   442→			slog.String("files_hash", filesHash[:12]),
   443→		)
   444→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Already reviewed these changes, skipping\n")
   445→		return
   446→	}
   447→
   448→	// Capture HEAD at trigger time so the detached review diffs against
   449→	// the correct commit even if HEAD moves during the initial delay.
   450→	payload.BaseCommit = resolveHEAD(repoRoot)
   451→	logging.Debug(logCtx, "wingman captured base commit",
   452→		slog.String("base_commit", payload.BaseCommit),
   453→	)
   454→
   455→	// Write payload to a temp file instead of passing as a CLI argument,
   456→	// which can exceed OS argv limits (~128KB Linux, ~256KB macOS) with
   457→	// many files or long prompts.
   458→	payloadJSON, err := json.Marshal(payload)
   459→	if err != nil {
   460→		logging.Error(logCtx, "wingman failed to marshal payload", slog.Any("error", err))
   461→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Failed to marshal payload: %v\n", err)
   462→		_ = os.Remove(lockPath)
   463→		return
   464→	}
   465→	payloadPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, ".entire", "wingman-payload.json")
   466→	//nolint:gosec // G306: payload file is not secrets
   467→	if err := os.WriteFile(payloadPath, payloadJSON, 0o644); err != nil {
   468→		logging.Error(logCtx, "wingman failed to write payload file", slog.Any("error", err))
   469→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[wingman] Failed to write payload file: %v\n", err)
   470→		_ = os.Remove(lockPath)
   471→		return
   472→	}
   473→
   474→	// Spawn detached review process with path to payload file
```
